elefant_foot_compensation.label: Elephant foot compensation
elefant_foot_compensation.tooltip: The first layer will be shrunk in the XY plane by the configured value to compensate for the 1st layer squish aka an Elephant Foot effect.

thumbnails.label: G-code thumbnails
thumbnails.tooltip:
Picture sizes to be stored into a .gcode / .bgcode and .sl1 / .sl1s files, in the following format: "XxY/EXT, XxY/EXT, ..."
Currently supported extensions are PNG, QOI, JPG, BTT_TFT and COLPIC.

thumbnails_format.label: Format of G-code thumbnails
thumbnails_format.tooltip: Format of G-code thumbnails: PNG for best quality, JPG for smallest size, QOI for low memory firmware, BTT_TFT for BigTreeTech touchscreens, COLPIC for Elegoo Neptune-series on-screen previews

layer_height.label: Layer height
layer_height.tooltip:
This setting controls the layer height used throughout the slice, except for the first layer. Thinner layers give better accuracy but take more time to print. When the height that fits a whole number of layers into 1 mm is a repeating decimal, enter the rounded value and it is used as the exact fraction, so the layers stay aligned to millimeter boundaries:

0.3333 = 3 layers/mm
0.1667 = 6 layers/mm
0.1429 = 7 layers/mm
0.1111 = 9 layers/mm

1, 2, 4, 5, 8, and 10 layers/mm are exact decimals and are used as entered.

color_mixing_base_layers.label: Color mixing base layers
color_mixing_base_layers.tooltip: Number of initial layers that print with a single filament instead of color-mixed dither. The bottom of a print is exposed (glass beds, flipped prints) and the dither pattern produces visible striping until the cycle has had several layers to converge. Locking the base to one filament also keeps bed adhesion uniform on the most critical layers. Set to 0 to disable and start color mixing immediately on layer 1.

color_mixing_base_extruder.label: Color mixing base filament
color_mixing_base_extruder.tooltip:
Which loaded filament to use for the color mixing base layers (see above).
• Darkest: auto-pick the darkest loaded filament. Hides any dither artifacts and tends to give the cleanest-looking bottom face.
• Lightest: auto-pick the brightest loaded filament. Useful when the bottom of the print should look bright or be barely visible.
• Volume default: use whatever filament the volume is otherwise assigned to. Pick this if you want explicit control through the volume's extruder setting.

max_print_height.label: Max print height
max_print_height.tooltip: Set this to the maximum height that can be reached by your extruder while printing.

print_host.label: Hostname, IP or URL
print_host.tooltip: Slic3r can upload G-code files to a printer host. This field should contain the hostname, IP address or URL of the printer host instance. Print host behind HAProxy with basic auth enabled can be accessed by putting the user name and password into the URL in the following format: https://username:password@your-octopi-address/

printhost_apikey.label: API Key / Password
printhost_apikey.tooltip: Slic3r can upload G-code files to a printer host. This field should contain the API Key or the password required for authentication.

printhost_cafile.label: HTTPS CA File
printhost_cafile.tooltip: Custom CA certificate file can be specified for HTTPS OctoPrint connections, in crt/pem format. If left blank, the default OS CA certificate repository is used.

printhost_ssl_ignore_revoke.label: Ignore HTTPS certificate revocation checks
printhost_ssl_ignore_revoke.tooltip: Ignore HTTPS certificate revocation checks in case of missing or offline distribution points. One may want to enable this option for self signed certificates if connection fails.

preset_names.label: Printer preset names
preset_names.tooltip: Names of presets related to the physical printer

arc_fitting.label: Arc fitting
arc_fitting.tooltip: Enable to get a G-code file which has G2 and G3 moves. G-code resolution will be used as the fitting tolerance.

automatic_extrusion_widths.label: Auto extrusion widths
automatic_extrusion_widths.tooltip: Automatically calculates extrusion widths based on the nozzle diameter of the currently used extruder. This setting is essential for printing with different nozzle diameters.

automatic_infill_combination.label: Automatic infill combination
automatic_infill_combination.tooltip: This feature automatically combines infill of several layers and speeds up your print by extruding thicker infill layers while preserving thin perimeters, thus maintaining accuracy. Note: Combined layer height cannot exceed the nozzle diameter.

automatic_infill_combination_max_layer_h.label: Automatic infill combination - Max layer height
automatic_infill_combination_max_layer_h.fullLabel: Automatic infill combination - Max layer height
automatic_infill_combination_max_layer_h.tooltip: Maximum layer height for combining infill when automatic infill combining is enabled. Maximum layer height could be specified either as an absolute in millimeters value or as a percentage of nozzle diameter. For printing with different nozzle diameters, it is recommended to use percentage value over absolute value.

avoid_crossing_curled_overhangs.label: Avoid crossing curled overhangs (Experimental)
avoid_crossing_curled_overhangs.tooltip: Plan travel moves such that the extruder avoids areas where the filament may be curled up. This is mostly happening on steeper rounded overhangs and may cause a crash with the nozzle. This feature slows down both the print and the G-code generation.

avoid_crossing_perimeters.label: Avoid crossing perimeters
avoid_crossing_perimeters.tooltip: Optimize travel moves in order to minimize the crossing of perimeters. This is mostly useful with Bowden extruders which suffer from oozing. This feature slows down both the print and the G-code generation.

avoid_crossing_perimeters_max_detour.label: Avoid crossing perimeters - Max detour length
avoid_crossing_perimeters_max_detour.fullLabel: Avoid crossing perimeters - Max detour length
avoid_crossing_perimeters_max_detour.tooltip: The maximum detour length for avoid crossing perimeters. If the detour is longer than this value, avoid crossing perimeters is not applied for this travel path. Detour length could be specified either as an absolute value or as percentage (for example 50%) of a direct travel path. Set to zero to disable.

bed_temperature.label: Other layers
bed_temperature.tooltip: Bed temperature for layers after the first one. Set this to zero to keep the first layer bed temperature for the entire print.

chamber_temperature.label: Nominal
chamber_temperature.tooltip:
Required chamber temperature for the print.
When set to zero, the nominal chamber temperature is not set in the G-code.

chamber_minimal_temperature.label: Minimal
chamber_minimal_temperature.tooltip:
Minimal chamber temperature that the printer waits for before the print starts. This allows to start the print before the nominal chamber temperature is reached.
When set to zero, the minimal chamber temperature is not set in the G-code.

bed_temperature_extruder.label: Bed temperature by extruder
bed_temperature_extruder.tooltip: The extruder which determines bed temperatures. Set to 0 to determine temperatures based on the first printing extruder of the first and the second layers.

before_layer_gcode.label: Before layer change G-code
before_layer_gcode.tooltip: This custom code is inserted at every layer change, right before the Z move. Note that you can use placeholder variables for all Slic3r settings as well as [layer_num] and [layer_z].

between_objects_gcode.label: Between objects G-code
between_objects_gcode.tooltip: This code is inserted between objects when using sequential printing. By default extruder and bed temperature are reset using non-wait command; however if M104, M109, M140 or M190 are detected in this custom code, Slic3r will not add temperature commands. Note that you can use placeholder variables for all Slic3r settings, so you can put a "M109 S[first_layer_temperature]" command wherever you want.

bottom_solid_layers.label: BottomLayers
bottom_solid_layers.tooltip: Number of solid layers to generate on bottom surfaces.

bottom_solid_min_thickness.label: BottomLayers
bottom_solid_min_thickness.tooltip: The number of bottom solid layers is increased above bottom_solid_layers if necessary to satisfy minimum thickness of bottom shell.

bridge_acceleration.label: Bridge
bridge_acceleration.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for bridges. Set zero to disable acceleration control for bridges.

bridge_angle.label: Bridging angle
bridge_angle.tooltip: Bridging angle override. If left to zero, the bridging angle will be calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided angle will be used for all bridges. Use 180° for zero angle.

counterbore_bridge_layers.label: Counterbore bridge layers
counterbore_bridge_layers.tooltip: Number of transition layers for counterbore bridge regions painted with Ctrl+K. Each layer bridges from a rotated direction, progressively closing the hole. More layers produce a gentler overhang angle.

bridge_fan_speed.label: Bridge infill
bridge_fan_speed.tooltip: Fan speed for bridge infill extrusions. Used in both auto cooling and manual fan control modes.

enable_manual_fan_speeds.label: Enable manual fan speeds
enable_manual_fan_speeds.tooltip: When enabled, use the manual fan speed values below for each feature type. This disables dynamic overhang fan speeds to prevent conflicting fan commands. Useful for fine-tuned control over fan behavior per feature.

manual_fan_speed_overhang_perimeter.label: Overhang perimeters
manual_fan_speed_overhang_perimeter.tooltip: Fan speed for overhang perimeters. Used in both auto cooling and manual fan modes. In auto mode, this overrides the bridge fan speed specifically for overhang perimeters. Set to 0 to use no fan for this feature type.

manual_fan_speed_interlocking_perimeter.label: Interlocking perimeters
manual_fan_speed_interlocking_perimeter.tooltip: Fan speed for interlocking perimeters when auto cooling is disabled. Set to 0 to use no fan for this feature type.

manual_fan_speed_serpentine.label: Serpentine
manual_fan_speed_serpentine.tooltip: Fan speed for serpentine extrusions when auto cooling is disabled. Set to 0 to use no fan for this feature type.

manual_fan_speed_serpentine_overhang.label: Serpentine overhang
manual_fan_speed_serpentine_overhang.tooltip: Fan speed for overhanging serpentine extrusions when auto cooling is disabled. Set to 0 to use no fan for this feature type.

manual_fan_speed_external_perimeter.label: External perimeters
manual_fan_speed_external_perimeter.tooltip: Fan speed for external perimeters when auto cooling is disabled. Set to 0 to use no fan for this feature type.

manual_fan_speed_perimeter.label: Internal perimeters
manual_fan_speed_perimeter.tooltip: Fan speed for internal perimeters when auto cooling is disabled. Set to 0 to use no fan for this feature type.

manual_fan_speed_top_solid_infill.label: Top solid infill
manual_fan_speed_top_solid_infill.tooltip: Fan speed for top solid infill when auto cooling is disabled. Set to 0 to use no fan for this feature type.

manual_fan_speed_solid_infill.label: Solid infill
manual_fan_speed_solid_infill.tooltip: Fan speed for solid infill (not top) when auto cooling is disabled. Set to 0 to use no fan for this feature type.

manual_fan_speed_internal_infill.label: Sparse infill
manual_fan_speed_internal_infill.tooltip: Fan speed for sparse internal infill when auto cooling is disabled. Set to 0 to use no fan for this feature type.

manual_fan_speed_ironing.label: Ironing
manual_fan_speed_ironing.tooltip: Fan speed for ironing passes when auto cooling is disabled. Set to 0 to use no fan for this feature type.

manual_fan_speed_skirt.label: Skirt/Brim
manual_fan_speed_skirt.tooltip: Fan speed for skirt and brim when auto cooling is disabled. Set to 0 to use no fan for this feature type.

manual_fan_speed_support_material.label: Support material
manual_fan_speed_support_material.tooltip: Fan speed for support material when auto cooling is disabled. Set to 0 to use no fan for this feature type.

manual_fan_speed_support_interface.label: Support interface
manual_fan_speed_support_interface.tooltip: Fan speed for support interface when auto cooling is disabled. Set to 0 to use no fan for this feature type.

bridge_flow_ratio.label: Bridge flow ratio
bridge_flow_ratio.tooltip: This factor affects the amount of plastic for bridging. You can decrease it slightly to pull the extrudates and prevent sagging, although default settings are usually good and you should experiment with cooling (use a fan) before tweaking this.

bridge_extrusion_width.label: Bridge infill
bridge_extrusion_width.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for bridges. Bridges print in mid-air and cannot squish against a layer below, so using a narrower width (around nozzle diameter) produces better results than the wider solid infill width. If left zero, solid infill extrusion width will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 110%) it will be computed over nozzle diameter or layer height, depending on the 'Percentages relative to nozzle size' setting.

top_one_perimeter_type.label: Single perimeter on top surfaces
top_one_perimeter_type.tooltip: Use only one perimeter on flat top surface, to give more space to the top infill pattern. Could be applied on topmost surface or all top surfaces.

only_one_perimeter_first_layer.label: Only one perimeter on first layer
only_one_perimeter_first_layer.fullLabel: Only one perimeter on first layer
only_one_perimeter_first_layer.tooltip: Use only one perimeter on the first layer.

over_bridge_speed.label: Over bridges
over_bridge_speed.tooltip: Speed for printing solid infill above bridges. Set to 0 to use solid infill speed. If set as percentage, the speed is calculated over solid infill speed.

enable_dynamic_overhang_speeds.label: Enable dynamic overhang speeds
enable_dynamic_overhang_speeds.tooltip: This setting enables dynamic speed control on overhangs.

enable_dynamic_fan_speeds.label: Enable dynamic fan speeds
enable_dynamic_fan_speeds.tooltip: This setting enables dynamic fan speed control on overhangs.

brim_width.label: Brim width
brim_width.tooltip: The horizontal width of the brim that will be printed around each object on the first layer. When raft is used, no brim is generated (use raft_first_layer_expansion).

brim_type.label: Brim type
brim_type.tooltip: The places where the brim will be printed around each object on the first layer.

brim_separation.label: Brim separation gap
brim_separation.tooltip: Offset of brim from the printed object. The offset is applied after the elephant foot compensation.

brim_ears_max_angle.label: Brim ear max angle
brim_ears_max_angle.tooltip: Maximum angle to let a brim ear appear. If set to 0, no brim will be created. If set to ~180, brim will be created on everything but straight sections.

brim_ears_detection_length.label: Brim ear detection radius
brim_ears_detection_length.tooltip: The geometry will be decimated before detecting sharp angles. This parameter indicates the minimum length of the deviation for the decimation. 0 to deactivate.

colorprint_heights.label: Colorprint height
colorprint_heights.tooltip: Heights at which a filament change is to occur.

compatible_printers_condition.label: Compatible printers condition
compatible_printers_condition.tooltip: A boolean expression using the configuration values of an active printer profile. If this expression evaluates to true, this profile is considered compatible with the active printer profile.

compatible_prints_condition.label: Compatible print profiles condition
compatible_prints_condition.tooltip: A boolean expression using the configuration values of an active print profile. If this expression evaluates to true, this profile is considered compatible with the active print profile.

complete_objects.label: Complete individual objects
complete_objects.tooltip: When printing multiple objects or copies, this feature will complete each object before moving onto next one (and starting it from its bottom layer). This feature is useful to avoid the risk of ruined prints. Slic3r should warn and prevent you from extruder collisions, but beware.

cooling.label: Enable auto cooling
cooling.tooltip: This flag enables the automatic cooling logic that adjusts print speed and fan speed according to layer printing time.

cooling_slowdown_logic.label: Cooling slowdown logic
cooling_slowdown_logic.tooltip: Determines how the printer slows down layer printing when the minimum layer time isn't reached. 'Consistent surface' first tries to preserve the print speeds of the first two perimeters by slowing all other features. Only if this isn't sufficient, it also slows down those first two perimeters. 'Uniform cooling' slows down all print features, including the first two perimeters.

cooling_perimeter_transition_distance.label: Perimeter transition distance
cooling_perimeter_transition_distance.tooltip: Distance in millimeters before non-slowed perimeters where the original unslowed print speed is restored. This reduces print quality issues when transitioning from heavily slowed feature to fast perimeter printing.

cooling_tube_retraction.label: Cooling tube position
cooling_tube_retraction.tooltip: Distance of the center-point of the cooling tube from the extruder tip.

cooling_tube_length.label: Cooling tube length
cooling_tube_length.tooltip: Length of the cooling tube to limit space for cooling moves inside it.

default_acceleration.label: Default
default_acceleration.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will be reset to after the role-specific acceleration values are used (perimeter/infill). Set zero to prevent resetting acceleration at all.

default_filament_profile.label: Default filament profile
default_filament_profile.tooltip: Default filament profile associated with the current printer profile. On selection of the current printer profile, this filament profile will be activated.

default_print_profile.label: Default print profile
default_print_profile.tooltip: Default print profile associated with the current printer profile. On selection of the current printer profile, this print profile will be activated.

disable_fan_first_layers.label: Disable fan for the first
disable_fan_first_layers.tooltip: You can set this to a positive value to disable fan at all during the first layers, so that it does not make adhesion worse.

dont_support_bridges.label: Don't support bridges
dont_support_bridges.tooltip: Experimental option for preventing support material from being generated under bridged areas.

duplicate_distance.label: Distance between copies
duplicate_distance.tooltip: Distance used for the auto-arrange feature of the plater.

end_gcode.label: End G-code
end_gcode.tooltip: This end procedure is inserted at the end of the output file. Note that you can use placeholder variables for all preFlight settings.

end_filament_gcode.label: End G-code
end_filament_gcode.tooltip: This end procedure is inserted at the end of the output file, before the printer end gcode (and before any toolchange from this filament in case of multimaterial printers). Note that you can use placeholder variables for all preFlight settings. If you have multiple extruders, the gcode is processed in extruder order.

ensure_vertical_shell_thickness.label: Ensure vertical shell thickness
ensure_vertical_shell_thickness.tooltip: Add solid infill near sloping surfaces to guarantee the vertical shell thickness (top+bottom solid layers).

top_fill_pattern.label: Top solid fill pattern
top_fill_pattern.tooltip: Fill pattern for top infill. This only affects the top visible layer, and not its adjacent solid shells.

bottom_fill_pattern.label: Bottom solid fill pattern
bottom_fill_pattern.tooltip: Fill pattern for bottom infill. This only affects the bottom external visible layer, and not its adjacent solid shells.

external_perimeter_extrusion_width.label: External perimeters
external_perimeter_extrusion_width.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for external perimeters. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise 1.125 x nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 200%), it will be computed over nozzle diameter or layer height, depending on the 'Percentages relative to nozzle size' setting.

external_perimeter_speed.label: External perimeters
external_perimeter_speed.tooltip: This separate setting will affect the speed of external perimeters (the visible ones). If expressed as percentage (for example: 80%) it will be calculated on the perimeters speed setting above. Set to zero for auto.

external_perimeters_first.label: External perimeters first
external_perimeters_first.tooltip: Print contour perimeters from the outermost one to the innermost one instead of the default inverse order.

extra_perimeters.label: Extra perimeters if needed
extra_perimeters.tooltip: Add more perimeters when needed for avoiding gaps in sloping walls. Slic3r keeps adding perimeters, until more than 70% of the loop immediately above is supported.

extra_perimeters_on_overhangs.label: Extra perimeters on overhangs (Experimental)
extra_perimeters_on_overhangs.tooltip: Detect overhang areas where bridges cannot be anchored, and fill them with extra perimeter paths. These paths are anchored to the nearby non-overhang area when possible.

extruder.label: Extruder
extruder.tooltip: The extruder to use (unless more specific extruder settings are specified). This value overrides perimeter and infill extruders, but not the support extruders.

extruder_clearance_height.label: Height
extruder_clearance_height.tooltip:
Only used when 'Print Settings -> Complete individual objects' is active. Set this to the vertical distance between your nozzle tip and (usually) the X carriage rods. Used to check for collisions with previously printed objects and to prevent them when arranging.
The value is ignored for printers that come with more detailed extruder models.

extruder_clearance_radius.label: Radius
extruder_clearance_radius.tooltip:
Only used when 'Print Settings -> Complete individual objects' is active. Set this to a radius of a nozzle-centered cylinder big enough to enclose the extruder assembly. Used to check for collisions with previously printed objects and to prevent them when arranging.
The value is ignored for printers that come with more detailed extruder models.

extruder_colour.label: Extruder color
extruder_colour.tooltip: This is only used in the Slic3r interface as a visual help.

extruder_offset.label: Extruder offset
extruder_offset.tooltip: If your firmware doesn't handle the extruder displacement you need the G-code to take it into account. This option lets you specify the displacement of each extruder with respect to the first one. It expects positive coordinates (they will be subtracted from the XY coordinate).

extrusion_axis.label: Extrusion axis
extrusion_axis.tooltip: Use this option to set the axis letter associated to your printer's extruder (usually E but some printers use A).

extrusion_multiplier.label: Extrusion multiplier
extrusion_multiplier.tooltip: This factor changes the amount of flow proportionally. You may need to tweak this setting to get nice surface finish and correct single wall widths. Usual values are between 0.9 and 1.1. If you think you need to change this more, check filament diameter and your firmware E steps.

extrusion_width_percent_of_nozzle.label: Percentages relative to nozzle size
extrusion_width_percent_of_nozzle.tooltip: When enabled, percentage values in extrusion width fields are computed as a percentage of the nozzle diameter. When disabled, they are computed as a percentage of the layer height (legacy behavior).

extrusion_width.label: Default extrusion width
extrusion_width.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to allow a manual extrusion width. If left to zero, extrusion widths are derived from the nozzle diameter (see the tooltips for perimeter extrusion width, infill extrusion width etc). If expressed as percentage (for example: 230%), it will be computed over nozzle diameter or layer height, depending on the 'Percentages relative to nozzle size' setting.

fan_always_on.label: Keep fan always on
fan_always_on.tooltip: If this is enabled, fan will never be disabled and will be kept running at least at its minimum speed. Useful for PLA, harmful for ABS.

fan_below_layer_time.label: Enable fan if layer print time is below
fan_below_layer_time.fullLabel: Enable fan if layer print time is below
fan_below_layer_time.tooltip: If layer print time is estimated below this number of seconds, fan will be enabled and its speed will be calculated by interpolating the minimum and maximum speeds.

fan_spinup_time.label: Spin-up time
fan_spinup_time.tooltip: Time in milliseconds for the part cooling fan to spin up from 0% to 100%. This enables physics-based fan speed compensation: fan commands are issued earlier so the fan reaches target speed exactly when needed (e.g., at overhang/bridge start). The actual lead time is calculated proportionally based on the speed change magnitude. Set to 0 to disable this feature. Typical values: 300-1000ms for small blower fans, check your fan's datasheet or measure.

fan_spinup_response_type.label: Fan response type
fan_spinup_response_type.tooltip:
Acceleration profile of your part cooling fan. Affects how early the fan command is issued.
• Axial fan: Fast response, typical small axial fans
• Blower: Moderate response, typical small radial blowers
• High-inertia: Slow response, high-static-pressure blowers

fan_spinup_bridge_infill.label: Bridge infill
fan_spinup_bridge_infill.tooltip: Enable early fan spin-up before bridge infill. When enabled, the fan command is issued early enough for the fan to reach target speed before the bridge begins. Requires Spin-up time > 0.

fan_spinup_overhang_perimeter.label: Overhang perimeters
fan_spinup_overhang_perimeter.tooltip: Enable early fan spin-up before overhang perimeters. When enabled, the fan command is issued early enough for the fan to reach target speed before the overhang begins. Requires Spin-up time > 0.

fan_spinup_serpentine_overhang.label: Serpentine overhang
fan_spinup_serpentine_overhang.tooltip: Enable early fan spin-up before overhanging serpentine extrusions. When enabled, the fan command is issued early enough for the fan to reach target speed before the overhang begins. Requires Spin-up time > 0.

filament_colour.label: Color
filament_colour.tooltip: This is only used in the Slic3r interface as a visual help.

filament_transmission_distance.label: Transmission distance
filament_transmission_distance.tooltip: How deep light penetrates this filament before it appears fully opaque, in millimetres. Lower values = more opaque (the filament's color saturates over a thinner stack of layers). Higher values = more translucent (color builds up gradually as more material stacks on top). Color Mixing uses this to predict the blended color of stacked filament layers, so accurate values produce accurate previews. Measure with the preFlight TD1S sensor for precise results, or leave at the 4.0 default if you have not measured -- this works reasonably for most opaque PLA but can be off for translucent, silk, or specialty filaments.

filament_notes.label: Filament notes
filament_notes.tooltip: You can put your notes regarding the filament here.

filament_max_volumetric_speed.label: Max volumetric flow
filament_max_volumetric_speed.tooltip: Maximum volumetric flow (mm³/s) this filament can sustain. Used by Auto speed to calculate print move speeds. Also caps all print speeds regardless of Auto speed.

filament_max_volumetric_flow.label: Max volumetric flow
filament_max_volumetric_flow.tooltip: Maximum volumetric flow (mm³/s) this filament can sustain. Used by Auto speed to calculate print move speeds. Also caps all print speeds regardless of Auto speed.

filament_max_print_speed.label: Max print speed
filament_max_print_speed.tooltip: Overrides the print profile's Max print speed for auto speed calculations. Set to zero to use the print profile's value.

filament_infill_max_speed.label: Max non-crossing infill speed
filament_infill_max_speed.tooltip: Maximum speed allowed for this filament while printing infill without any self intersections in a single layer. Set to zero for no limit.

filament_infill_max_crossing_speed.label: Max crossing infill speed
filament_infill_max_crossing_speed.tooltip: Maximum speed allowed for this filament while printing infill with self intersections in a single layer. Set to zero for no limit.

filament_loading_speed.label: Loading speed
filament_loading_speed.tooltip: Speed used for loading the filament on the wipe tower.

filament_loading_speed_start.label: Loading speed at the start
filament_loading_speed_start.tooltip: Speed used at the very beginning of loading phase.

filament_unloading_speed.label: Unloading speed
filament_unloading_speed.tooltip: Speed used for unloading the filament on the wipe tower (does not affect  initial part of unloading just after ramming).

filament_unloading_speed_start.label: Unloading speed at the start
filament_unloading_speed_start.tooltip: Speed used for unloading the tip of the filament immediately after ramming.

filament_toolchange_delay.label: Delay after unloading
filament_toolchange_delay.tooltip: Time to wait after the filament is unloaded. May help to get reliable toolchanges with flexible materials that may need more time to shrink to original dimensions.

filament_stamping_distance.label: Stamping distance measured from the center of the cooling tube
filament_stamping_distance.fullLabel: Stamping distance measured from the center of the cooling tube
filament_stamping_distance.tooltip: If set to nonzero value, filament is moved toward the nozzle between the individual cooling moves ("stamping"). This option configures how long this movement should be before the filament is retracted again.

filament_cooling_moves.label: Number of cooling moves
filament_cooling_moves.tooltip: Filament is cooled by being moved back and forth in the cooling tubes. Specify desired number of these moves.

filament_cooling_initial_speed.label: Speed of the first cooling move
filament_cooling_initial_speed.fullLabel: Speed of the first cooling move
filament_cooling_initial_speed.tooltip: Cooling moves are gradually accelerating beginning at this speed.

filament_minimal_purge_on_wipe_tower.label: Minimal purge on wipe tower
filament_minimal_purge_on_wipe_tower.tooltip: After a tool change, the exact position of the newly loaded filament inside the nozzle may not be known, and the filament pressure is likely not yet stable. Before purging the print head into an infill or a sacrificial object, Slic3r will always prime this amount of material into the wipe tower to produce successive infill or sacrificial object extrusions reliably.

filament_cooling_final_speed.label: Speed of the last cooling move
filament_cooling_final_speed.fullLabel: Speed of the last cooling move
filament_cooling_final_speed.tooltip: Cooling moves are gradually accelerating towards this speed.

filament_purge_multiplier.label: Purge volume multiplier
filament_purge_multiplier.tooltip: Purging volume on the wipe tower is determined by 'multimaterial_purging' in Printer Settings. This option allows to modify the volume on filament level. Note that the project can override this by setting project-specific values.

filament_load_time.label: Filament load time
filament_load_time.tooltip: Time for the printer firmware (or the Multi Material Unit 2.0) to load a new filament during a tool change (when executing the T code). This time is added to the total print time by the G-code time estimator.

filament_ramming_parameters.label: Ramming parameters
filament_ramming_parameters.tooltip: This string is edited by RammingDialog and contains ramming specific parameters.

filament_unload_time.label: Filament unload time
filament_unload_time.tooltip: Time for the printer firmware (or the Multi Material Unit 2.0) to unload a filament during a tool change (when executing the T code). This time is added to the total print time by the G-code time estimator.

filament_multitool_ramming.label: Enable ramming for multitool setups
filament_multitool_ramming.tooltip: Perform ramming when using multitool printer (i.e. when the 'Single Extruder Multimaterial' in Printer Settings is unchecked). When checked, a small amount of filament is rapidly extruded on the wipe tower just before the toolchange. This option is only used when the wipe tower is enabled.

filament_multitool_ramming_volume.label: Multitool ramming volume
filament_multitool_ramming_volume.tooltip: The volume to be rammed before the toolchange.

filament_multitool_ramming_flow.label: Multitool ramming flow
filament_multitool_ramming_flow.tooltip: Flow used for ramming the filament before the toolchange.

filament_diameter.label: Diameter
filament_diameter.tooltip: Enter your filament diameter here. Good precision is required, so use a caliper and do multiple measurements along the filament, then compute the average.

filament_density.label: Density
filament_density.tooltip: Enter your filament density here. This is only for statistical information. A decent way is to weigh a known length of filament and compute the ratio of the length to volume. Better is to calculate the volume directly through displacement.

filament_type.label: Filament type
filament_type.tooltip: The filament material type for use in custom G-codes.

filament_soluble.label: Soluble material
filament_soluble.tooltip: Soluble material is most likely used for a soluble support.

filament_abrasive.label: Abrasive material
filament_abrasive.tooltip: This flag means that the material is abrasive and requires a hardened nozzle. The value is used by the printer to check it.

filament_enable_pressure_advance.label: Enable pressure advance
filament_enable_pressure_advance.tooltip:
Enable automatic pressure advance command emission for this filament. When enabled, the appropriate firmware command is inserted after the start filament G-code using the value below.

RepRapFirmware: M572 D<extruder> S<value>
Klipper: SET_PRESSURE_ADVANCE ADVANCE=<value>
Marlin: M900 K<value>

filament_pressure_advance.label: Pressure advance
filament_pressure_advance.tooltip: Pressure advance value for this filament. Higher values compensate for more flexible filament or longer Bowden tubes. Typical values range from 0.01 to 0.15 for direct drive and 0.3 to 1.0 for Bowden.

filament_cost.label: Cost
filament_cost.tooltip: Enter your filament cost per kg here. This is only for statistical information.

filament_spool_weight.label: Spool weight
filament_spool_weight.tooltip: Enter weight of the empty filament spool. One may weigh a partially consumed filament spool before printing and one may compare the measured weight with the calculated weight of the filament with the spool to find out whether the amount of filament on the spool is sufficient to finish the print.

filament_shrinkage_compensation_x.label: Shrinkage compensation X
filament_shrinkage_compensation_x.tooltip: Enter your filament shrinkage percentage for the X axis here to apply scaling of the object to compensate for shrinkage in the X axis. For example, if you measured 99mm instead of 100mm, enter 1%.

filament_shrinkage_compensation_y.label: Shrinkage compensation Y
filament_shrinkage_compensation_y.tooltip: Enter your filament shrinkage percentage for the Y axis here to apply scaling of the object to compensate for shrinkage in the Y axis. For example, if you measured 99mm instead of 100mm, enter 1%.

filament_shrinkage_compensation_z.label: Shrinkage compensation Z
filament_shrinkage_compensation_z.tooltip: Enter your filament shrinkage percentages for the Z axis here to apply scaling of the object to compensate for shrinkage in the Z axis. For example, if you measured 99mm instead of 100mm, enter 1%.

fill_angle.label: Fill angle
fill_angle.tooltip: Default base angle for infill orientation. Cross-hatching will be applied to this. Bridges will be infilled using the best direction Slic3r can detect, so this setting does not affect them.

fill_density.label: Sparse fill density
fill_density.tooltip: Density of sparse infill, expressed in the range 0% - 100%.

solid_fill_pattern.label: Solid fill pattern
solid_fill_pattern.tooltip: Fill pattern for solid infill (internal solid layers and vertical shells). Does not affect bridges.

first_layer_acceleration.label: First layer
first_layer_acceleration.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for first layer. Set zero to disable acceleration control for first layer.

first_layer_acceleration_over_raft.label: First object layer over raft interface
first_layer_acceleration_over_raft.fullLabel: First object layer over raft interface
first_layer_acceleration_over_raft.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for first layer of object above raft interface. Set zero to disable acceleration control for first layer of object above raft interface.

first_layer_bed_temperature.label: First layer
first_layer_bed_temperature.tooltip: Heated build plate temperature for the first layer. Set this to zero to disable bed temperature control commands in the output.

first_layer_extrusion_width.label: First layer
first_layer_extrusion_width.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for first layer. You can use this to force fatter extrudates for better adhesion. If expressed as percentage (for example 120%) it will be computed over nozzle diameter or layer height, depending on the 'Percentages relative to nozzle size' setting. If set to zero, it will use the default extrusion width.

first_layer_height.label: First layer height
first_layer_height.tooltip: When printing with very low layer heights, you might still want to print a thicker bottom layer to improve adhesion and tolerance for non perfect build plates.

first_layer_speed.label: First layer speed
first_layer_speed.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to all the print moves of the first layer, regardless of their type. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will scale the default speeds.

first_layer_infill_speed.label: First layer solid infill speed
first_layer_infill_speed.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to the solid infill print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the solid infill speed (for example: 40% of the solid infill speed). Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

first_layer_travel_speed.label: First layer travel speed
first_layer_travel_speed.tooltip: If set to a non-zero value, this speed will be used for travel moves on the first layer. If expressed as a percentage, it will be calculated over the travel speed. Set to 0 to use the normal travel speed on the first layer.

first_layer_speed_over_raft.label: Speed of object first layer over raft interface
first_layer_speed_over_raft.fullLabel: Speed of object first layer over raft interface
first_layer_speed_over_raft.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to all the print moves of the first object layer above raft interface, regardless of their type. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will scale the default speeds.

first_layer_temperature.label: First layer
first_layer_temperature.tooltip: Nozzle temperature for the first layer. If you want to control temperature manually during print, set this to zero to disable temperature control commands in the output G-code.

full_fan_speed_layer.label: Full fan speed at layer
full_fan_speed_layer.tooltip: Fan speed will be ramped up linearly from zero at layer "disable_fan_first_layers" to maximum at layer "full_fan_speed_layer". "full_fan_speed_layer" will be ignored if lower than "disable_fan_first_layers", in which case the fan will be running at maximum allowed speed at layer "disable_fan_first_layers" + 1.

fuzzy_skin.label: Fuzzy skin (global)
fuzzy_skin.tooltip: Applies fuzzy skin to ALL surfaces of the model. Set to 'None' if you only want fuzzy skin on painted areas.

fuzzy_skin_thickness.label: Fuzzy skin thickness
fuzzy_skin_thickness.tooltip: The maximum distance that each skin point can be offset (both ways), measured perpendicular to the perimeter wall.

fuzzy_skin_point_dist.label: Fuzzy skin point distance
fuzzy_skin_point_dist.tooltip: Perimeters will be split into multiple segments by inserting Fuzzy skin points. Lowering the Fuzzy skin point distance will increase the number of randomly offset points on the perimeter wall.

fuzzy_skin_first_layer.label: Fuzzy skin on bottom layer
fuzzy_skin_first_layer.tooltip: When enabled, fuzzy skin is applied to all layers including the first layer (layer 0). When disabled, fuzzy skin is skipped on the first layer, giving a smooth bottom surface for better bed adhesion while maintaining the fuzzy texture on all other layers.

fuzzy_skin_noise_type.label: Noise type
fuzzy_skin_noise_type.tooltip: Type of noise algorithm to use for fuzzy skin displacement. Classic uses random noise (original behavior). Perlin and Billow create spatially coherent textures. Ridged creates sharp, jagged features. Voronoi creates cell-based patchwork patterns.

fuzzy_skin_mode.label: Fuzzy skin mode
fuzzy_skin_mode.tooltip: How fuzzy skin effect is applied. Displacement offsets the path perpendicular to the surface. Extrusion varies the extrusion width instead. Combined uses both displacement and extrusion variation.

fuzzy_skin_scale.label: Feature size
fuzzy_skin_scale.tooltip: The base size of coherent noise features in mm. Higher values create larger texture features. Only applies to Perlin, Billow, Ridged, and Voronoi noise types.

fuzzy_skin_octaves.label: Noise octaves
fuzzy_skin_octaves.tooltip: Number of noise instances with decreasing feature size that are summed together. More octaves add finer detail but increase computation time. Only applies to Perlin, Billow, and Ridged noise types.

fuzzy_skin_persistence.label: Noise persistence
fuzzy_skin_persistence.tooltip: Controls how quickly the amplitude decreases for each successive octave. Lower values result in smoother noise, higher values preserve more fine detail. Only applies to Perlin and Billow noise types.

fuzzy_skin_point_placement.label: Point placement
fuzzy_skin_point_placement.tooltip:
Algorithm used for placing fuzzy skin points along perimeters.

• Standard: Original algorithm, faster but may cut corners at larger point distances.
• Shape-following: Preserves corner vertices for better accuracy, especially at larger point distances.

fuzzy_skin_painted_perimeters.label: Painted fuzzy skin
fuzzy_skin_painted_perimeters.tooltip:
Controls which perimeters are affected in PAINTED fuzzy skin areas. This setting only applies when using the paint-on fuzzy skin tool.

• External perimeters: Only the outermost perimeter (perimeter 0).
• External perimeters +1: External plus 1 inner perimeter (perimeters 0-1).
• External perimeters +2: External plus 2 inner perimeters (perimeters 0-2).
• External perimeters +3: External plus 3 inner perimeters (perimeters 0-3).
• All perimeters: All perimeters regardless of depth.

fuzzy_skin_on_top.label: Fuzzy skin on top surfaces
fuzzy_skin_on_top.tooltip: When enabled, fuzzy skin is applied to all painted areas including top surfaces visible from above. When disabled, fuzzy skin is skipped on perimeters that are visible from the top of the print, giving a smooth finish on top layers while maintaining the fuzzy texture on vertical walls.

fuzzy_skin_visibility_detection.label: Visibility detection
fuzzy_skin_visibility_detection.tooltip:
Controls the sampling interval used to detect visibility boundaries on perimeters. When 'Fuzzy skin on top/bottom surfaces' is disabled, the slicer samples along each perimeter to find where visibility changes (e.g., where a wall meets an internal shelf).

• Precise (1mm): Highest accuracy, checks every 1mm. Best quality at boundaries.
• Standard (2mm): Good balance of accuracy and speed.
• Relaxed (4mm): Faster slicing, minor boundary imprecision.
• Minimal (8mm): Fastest slicing, noticeable imprecision at boundaries.

Lower values increase slicing time but improve accuracy at visibility boundaries.

perimeter_compression.label: Perimeter compression
perimeter_compression.tooltip:
Controls how narrow a center perimeter can be when Athena fills tight wall sections. When full-count perimeters don't quite fit, Athena can squeeze a narrower center bead into the remaining space. This setting determines how thin that center bead is allowed to be. More aggressive compression fills more gaps but produces thinner beads. This setting only applies to the Athena perimeter generator.

• Minimal: Center beads can narrow to 75% of perimeter width
• Moderate: Center beads can narrow to 50% of perimeter width
• Aggressive: Center beads can narrow to 25% of perimeter width

The floor is always 33% of nozzle diameter to ensure printability.

max_perimeter_width.label: Maximum width
max_perimeter_width.tooltip: Bead width ceiling for Athena-generated walls and fills, as a percentage of the nozzle diameter. When a wall is too wide for one bead, Athena stretches a single bead up to this limit and splits into two beads beyond it. Lower values split sooner; higher values allow wider single beads. The ceiling never reduces walls below the configured extrusion widths.

thin_wall_precision.label: Thin wall width precision
thin_wall_precision.tooltip:
Controls the rounding precision for thin wall extrusion widths. Athena measures the actual wall thickness and snaps it to a grid to reduce noise.

Finer values (0.001mm) track tapered geometry more smoothly but may produce visible width variation on constant-thickness walls.

Coarser values (0.1mm) produce consistent widths on uniform walls but step more coarsely on tapered geometry.

This setting only applies to the Athena perimeter generator.

gcode_comments.label: Verbose G-code
gcode_comments.tooltip: Enable this to get a commented G-code file, with each line explained by a descriptive text. If you print from SD card, the additional weight of the file could make your firmware slow down.

gcode_flavor.label: G-code flavor
gcode_flavor.tooltip: Some G/M-code commands, including temperature control and others, are not universal. Set this option to your printer's firmware to get a compatible output. The "No extrusion" flavor prevents preFlight from exporting any extrusion value at all.

gcode_label_objects.label: Label objects
gcode_label_objects.tooltip:
Selects whether labels should be exported at object boundaries and in what format.
OctoPrint = comments to be consumed by OctoPrint CancelObject plugin.
Firmware = firmware specific G-code (it will be chosen based on firmware flavor and it can end up to be empty).

This settings is NOT compatible with Single Extruder Multi Material setup and Wipe into Object / Wipe into Infill.

gcode_substitutions.label: G-code substitutions
gcode_substitutions.tooltip: Find / replace patterns in G-code lines and substitute them.

high_current_on_filament_swap.label: High extruder current on filament swap
high_current_on_filament_swap.fullLabel: High extruder current on filament swap
high_current_on_filament_swap.tooltip: It may be beneficial to increase the extruder motor current during the filament exchange sequence to allow for rapid ramming feed rates and to overcome resistance when loading a filament with an ugly shaped tip.

infill_acceleration.label: Infill
infill_acceleration.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for infill. Set zero to disable acceleration control for infill.

solid_infill_acceleration.label: Solid infill
solid_infill_acceleration.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for solid infill. Set zero to use the value for infill.

top_solid_infill_acceleration.label: Top solid infill
top_solid_infill_acceleration.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for top solid infill. Set zero to use the value for solid infill.

wipe_tower_acceleration.label: Wipe tower
wipe_tower_acceleration.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for wipe tower. Set zero to disable acceleration control for the wipe tower.

travel_acceleration.label: Travel
travel_acceleration.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for travel moves. Set zero to disable acceleration control for travel.

travel_short_distance_acceleration.label: Travel short distance acceleration
travel_short_distance_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration used for short travel moves. Short travel distance is determined by the retract_before_travel setting.

infill_every_layers.label: Combine infill every
infill_every_layers.tooltip: This feature allows to combine infill and speed up your print by extruding thicker infill layers while preserving thin perimeters, thus accuracy. Note: Combined layer height cannot exceed the nozzle diameter (e.g., with a 0.4mm nozzle and 0.2mm layer height, you can combine up to 2 layers).

infill_anchor.label: Length of the infill anchor
infill_anchor.tooltip: Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. preFlight tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than infill_anchor_max is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to this parameter, but no longer than anchor_length_max. Set this parameter to zero to disable anchoring perimeters connected to a single infill line.

infill_anchor_max.label: Maximum length of the infill anchor
infill_anchor_max.fullLabel: Maximum length of the infill anchor
infill_anchor_max.tooltip: Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. preFlight tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than this parameter is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to infill_anchor, but no longer than this parameter. Set this parameter to zero to disable anchoring.

infill_extruder.label: Infill extruder
infill_extruder.tooltip: The extruder to use when printing infill.

infill_extrusion_width.label: Infill
infill_extrusion_width.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for infill. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise 1.125 x nozzle diameter will be used. You may want to use fatter extrudates to speed up the infill and make your parts stronger. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over nozzle diameter or layer height, depending on the 'Percentages relative to nozzle size' setting.

infill_first.label: Infill before perimeters
infill_first.tooltip: This option will switch the print order of perimeters and infill, making the latter first.

external_perimeter_overlap.label: Ext. perimeter/perimeter overlap
external_perimeter_overlap.tooltip: Controls overlap between external perimeter and first inner perimeter. Extruded beads have rounded edges that must overlap for proper bonding. The default 10.73% is derived from the geometric constant (1 - π/4) / 2, which accounts for the semicircular bead cross-section. The overlap amount is calculated from layer height: at 10.73%, beads bond optimally; at 100%, beads completely overlap. Requires at least 2 perimeters.

perimeter_perimeter_overlap.label: Perimeter/perimeter overlap
perimeter_perimeter_overlap.tooltip: Controls overlap between all internal perimeters. Extruded beads have rounded edges that must overlap for proper bonding. The default 10.73% is derived from the geometric constant (1 - π/4) / 2, which accounts for the semicircular bead cross-section. The overlap amount is calculated from layer height: at 10.73%, beads bond optimally; at 100%, beads completely overlap. Requires at least 3 perimeters. Maximum 80%.

infill_overlap.label: Infill/perimeters overlap
infill_overlap.tooltip: Controls overlap between infill and the innermost perimeter. Extruded beads have rounded edges that must overlap for proper bonding. The default 21.46% is derived from the geometric constant (1 - π/4), which accounts for the semicircular bead cross-section. The overlap amount is calculated from layer height. Higher values may cause over-extrusion artifacts.

bridge_infill_overlap.label: Bridge infill overlap
bridge_infill_overlap.tooltip: Controls overlap between adjacent bridge infill lines. At 0% (default), lines touch edge-to-edge. Positive values create overlap (lines print closer, may help lines support each other). Negative values create gaps between lines. The overlap amount is calculated from layer height.

bridge_infill_perimeter_overlap.label: Bridge infill/perimeters overlap
bridge_infill_perimeter_overlap.tooltip: Controls overlap between bridge infill and the innermost perimeter. Separate from 'Infill/perimeters overlap' which affects normal infill. Extruded beads have rounded edges that must overlap for proper bonding. The default 21.46% is derived from the geometric constant (1 - π/4), which accounts for the semicircular bead cross-section. The overlap amount is calculated from layer height. At 0%, edges touch. Negative values create gaps.

infill_speed.label: Infill
infill_speed.tooltip: Speed for printing the internal fill. Set to zero for auto.

inherits.label: Inherits profile
inherits.tooltip: Name of the profile, from which this profile inherits.

interface_shells.label: Interface shells
interface_shells.tooltip: Force the generation of solid shells between adjacent materials/volumes. Useful for multi-extruder prints with translucent materials or manual soluble support material.

mmu_segmented_region_max_width.label: Maximum width of a segmented region
mmu_segmented_region_max_width.fullLabel: Maximum width of a segmented region
mmu_segmented_region_max_width.tooltip: Maximum width of a segmented region. Zero disables this feature.

mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth.label: Interlocking depth of a segmented region
mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth.fullLabel: Interlocking depth of a segmented region
mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth.tooltip: Interlocking depth of a segmented region. It will be ignored if "mmu_segmented_region_max_width" is zero or if "mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth"is bigger then "mmu_segmented_region_max_width". Zero disables this feature.

ironing.label: Enable ironing
ironing.tooltip: Enable ironing of the top layers with the hot print head for smooth surface

interlocking_beam.label: Use beam interlocking
interlocking_beam.tooltip: Generate interlocking beam structure at the locations where different filaments touch. This improves the adhesion between filaments, especially models printed in different materials.

interlocking_beam_width.label: Interlocking beam width
interlocking_beam_width.tooltip: The width of the interlocking structure beams.

interlocking_beam_layer_count.label: Interlocking beam layers
interlocking_beam_layer_count.tooltip: The height of the beams of the interlocking structure, measured in number of layers. Less layers is stronger, but more prone to defects.

interlocking_depth.label: Interlocking depth
interlocking_depth.tooltip: The distance from the boundary between filaments to generate interlocking structure, measured in cells. Too few cells will result in poor adhesion.

interlocking_boundary_avoidance.label: Interlocking boundary avoidance
interlocking_boundary_avoidance.tooltip: The distance from the outside of a model where interlocking structures will not be generated, measured in cells.

ironing_flowrate.label: Flow rate
ironing_flowrate.tooltip: Percent of a flow rate relative to object's normal layer height.

layer_gcode.label: After layer change G-code
layer_gcode.tooltip: This custom code is inserted at every layer change, right after the Z move and before the extruder moves to the first layer point. Note that you can use placeholder variables for all Slic3r settings as well as [layer_num] and [layer_z].

remaining_times.label: Supports remaining times
remaining_times.tooltip: Emit M73 P[percent printed] R[remaining time in minutes] at 1 minute intervals into the G-code to let the firmware show accurate remaining time. Some firmware (like Marlin) recognizes M73 for progress reporting. Also the i3 MK3 firmware supports M73 Qxx Sxx for the silent mode.

binary_gcode.label: Supports binary G-code
binary_gcode.tooltip: Enable, if the firmware supports binary G-code format (bgcode). To generate .bgcode files, make sure you have binary G-code enabled in Configuration->Preferences->Other.

machine_limits_usage.label: How to apply limits
machine_limits_usage.tooltip: How to apply the Machine Limits

machine_max_feedrate_x.label: Maximum feedrate X
machine_max_feedrate_x.tooltip: Maximum feedrate of the X axis

machine_max_feedrate_y.label: Maximum feedrate Y
machine_max_feedrate_y.tooltip: Maximum feedrate of the Y axis

machine_max_feedrate_z.label: Maximum feedrate Z
machine_max_feedrate_z.tooltip: Maximum feedrate of the Z axis

machine_max_feedrate_e.label: Maximum feedrate E
machine_max_feedrate_e.tooltip: Maximum feedrate of the E axis

machine_max_acceleration_x.label: Maximum acceleration X
machine_max_acceleration_x.tooltip: Maximum acceleration of the X axis

machine_max_acceleration_y.label: Maximum acceleration Y
machine_max_acceleration_y.tooltip: Maximum acceleration of the Y axis

machine_max_acceleration_z.label: Maximum acceleration Z
machine_max_acceleration_z.tooltip: Maximum acceleration of the Z axis

machine_max_acceleration_e.label: Maximum acceleration E
machine_max_acceleration_e.tooltip: Maximum acceleration of the E axis

machine_max_jerk_x.label: Maximum jerk X
machine_max_jerk_x.tooltip: Maximum jerk of the X axis

machine_max_jerk_y.label: Maximum jerk Y
machine_max_jerk_y.tooltip: Maximum jerk of the Y axis

machine_max_jerk_z.label: Maximum jerk Z
machine_max_jerk_z.tooltip: Maximum jerk of the Z axis

machine_max_jerk_e.label: Maximum jerk E
machine_max_jerk_e.tooltip: Maximum jerk of the E axis

machine_max_junction_deviation.label: Junction deviation
machine_max_junction_deviation.tooltip:
Junction deviation for Marlin 2.x firmware (M205 J).

When set to a value greater than 0, the slicer will use the junction deviation algorithm instead of classic jerk for time estimation and will output M205 J in the G-code.

Junction deviation provides more accurate cornering speed calculations by allowing the toolhead to deviate from the ideal path by this distance at corners.

Typical values: 0.01 - 0.08 mm
Set to 0 to use classic jerk (M205 XYZE).

machine_rrf_m566.label: M566 (Jerk)
machine_rrf_m566.tooltip:
Enter your M566 command from config.g.

Sets jerk (instantaneous speed change) limits in mm/min.
The P parameter controls jerk policy:
  P0 (default): Jerk only between consecutive extrusion or travel moves
  P1: Marlin-like behavior (jerk between any moves)

Default: M566 X900 Y900 Z600 E300 P0

machine_rrf_m201.label: M201 (Max Accel)
machine_rrf_m201.tooltip:
Enter your M201 command from config.g.

Sets maximum acceleration per axis in mm/s².

Default: M201 X1000 Y1000 Z200 E500

machine_rrf_m203.label: M203 (Max Speed)
machine_rrf_m203.tooltip:
Enter your M203 command from config.g.

Sets maximum feedrate per axis in mm/min (NOT mm/sec!).

Default: M203 X6000 Y6000 Z1200 E6000

machine_rrf_m204.label: M204 (Accel)
machine_rrf_m204.tooltip:
Enter your M204 command from config.g (optional).

Sets print and travel acceleration in mm/s².
  P = Print acceleration (with extrusion)
  T = Travel acceleration (without extrusion)

Optional - leave blank to let the M201 per-axis limits govern.

machine_rrf_m207.label: M207 (Retract)
machine_rrf_m207.tooltip:
Enter your M207 command from config.g (optional).

Sets firmware retraction parameters:
  S = Retract length (mm)
  F = Retract feedrate (mm/min)
  T = Unretract feedrate (mm/min)
  Z = Z-lift during retract (mm)
  R = Extra unretract length (mm)

Optional - leave blank if not using firmware retraction (G10/G11).

machine_klipper_max_velocity.label: Max velocity
machine_klipper_max_velocity.tooltip:
Maximum velocity from your Klipper printer.cfg [printer] section.

This is the global velocity limit for all moves.

Can be changed mid-print with:
  SET_VELOCITY_LIMIT VELOCITY=<value>

machine_klipper_max_accel.label: Max acceleration
machine_klipper_max_accel.tooltip:
Maximum acceleration from your Klipper printer.cfg [printer] section.

This is the global acceleration limit for all moves.

Can be changed mid-print with:
  SET_VELOCITY_LIMIT ACCEL=<value>
  M204 S<value>

machine_klipper_square_corner_velocity.label: Square corner velocity
machine_klipper_square_corner_velocity.tooltip:
Square corner velocity from your Klipper printer.cfg [printer] section.

Controls how fast the toolhead moves through corners.
Higher values allow faster cornering but may cause ringing.
Klipper default is 5.0 mm/s.

Can be changed mid-print with:
  SET_VELOCITY_LIMIT SQUARE_CORNER_VELOCITY=<value>

machine_klipper_minimum_cruise_ratio.label: Minimum cruise ratio
machine_klipper_minimum_cruise_ratio.tooltip:
Minimum cruise ratio from your Klipper printer.cfg [printer] section.

On short moves, the printer maintains at least this fraction
of the requested speed instead of decelerating fully.
Klipper default is 0.5 (50% of nominal speed).

Can be changed mid-print with:
  SET_VELOCITY_LIMIT MINIMUM_CRUISE_RATIO=<value>

machine_time_compensation.label: Real-World Compensation
machine_time_compensation.tooltip:
Adjusts time estimates to better match real-world print times.

Negative values increase the estimate (more conservative).
Positive values decrease the estimate (more aggressive).

Examples:
  -15% = Estimate will be 15% longer (recommended starting point)
  0% = No adjustment (pure physics calculation)
  +10% = Estimate will be 10% shorter

Adjust based on how your actual prints compare to estimates.

machine_max_acceleration_retracting.label: Maximum acceleration when retracting
machine_max_acceleration_retracting.tooltip:
Maximum acceleration when retracting.

Not used for RepRapFirmware, which does not support it.

max_fan_speed.label: Max
max_fan_speed.tooltip: This setting represents the maximum speed of your fan.

max_layer_height.label: Max
max_layer_height.tooltip: This is the highest printable layer height for this extruder, used to cap the variable layer height and support layer height. Maximum recommended layer height is 75% of the extrusion width to achieve reasonable inter-layer adhesion. If set to 0, layer height is limited to 75% of the nozzle diameter.

auto_speed.label: Auto speed
auto_speed.tooltip: When enabled, print move speeds are automatically calculated from each filament's max volumetric flow and capped at Max print speed. Bridge and small perimeter speeds remain manual (set to 0 for auto speed). Over-bridge set to 0 uses solid infill speed. Gap fill set to 0 disables it.

max_print_speed.label: Max print speed
max_print_speed.tooltip: The maximum speed for any print move when using auto speed, or the fallback speed when individual speeds are set to 0.

max_volumetric_speed.label: Max volumetric flow
max_volumetric_speed.tooltip: Print-level cap on volumetric flow. When greater than zero, it clamps each filament's Max volumetric flow if this value is lower, limiting auto speed accordingly. Set to 0 to rely solely on the filament's Max volumetric flow.

max_volumetric_flow.label: Max volumetric flow
max_volumetric_flow.tooltip: Print-level cap on volumetric flow. When greater than zero, it clamps each filament's Max volumetric flow if this value is lower, limiting auto speed accordingly. Set to 0 to rely solely on the filament's Max volumetric flow.

max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_posi.label: Max volumetric slope positive
max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_posi.tooltip: This experimental setting is used to limit the speed of change in extrusion rate for a transition from lower speed to higher speed. A value of 1.8 mm³/s² ensures, that a change from the extrusion rate of 1.8 mm³/s (0.45 mm extrusion width, 0.2 mm extrusion height, feedrate 20 mm/s) to 5.4 mm³/s (feedrate 60 mm/s) will take at least 2 seconds.

max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_nega.label: Max volumetric slope negative
max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_nega.tooltip: This experimental setting is used to limit the speed of change in extrusion rate for a transition from higher speed to lower speed. A value of 1.8 mm³/s² ensures, that a change from the extrusion rate of 5.4 mm³/s (0.45 mm extrusion width, 0.2 mm extrusion height, feedrate 60 mm/s) to 1.8 mm³/s (feedrate 20 mm/s) will take at least 2 seconds.

min_fan_speed.label: Min
min_fan_speed.tooltip: This setting represents the minimum PWM your fan needs to work.

min_layer_height.label: Min
min_layer_height.tooltip: This is the lowest printable layer height for this extruder and limits the resolution for variable layer height. Typical values are between 0.05 mm and 0.1 mm.

min_print_speed.label: Min print speed
min_print_speed.tooltip: Slic3r will not scale speed down below this speed.

min_skirt_length.label: Minimal filament extrusion length
min_skirt_length.tooltip: Generate no less than the number of skirt loops required to consume the specified amount of filament on the bottom layer. For multi-extruder machines, this minimum applies to each extruder.

notes.label: Configuration notes
notes.tooltip: You can put here your personal notes. This text will be added to the G-code header comments.

print_nozzle_diameters.label: Print nozzle diameters
print_nozzle_diameters.tooltip: Nozzle diameters for this print profile. When set, these values override the printer's nozzle diameters.

print_high_flow_nozzle.label: High flow nozzle
print_high_flow_nozzle.tooltip: Print preset-specific high flow nozzle settings

nozzle_diameter.label: Nozzle diameter
nozzle_diameter.tooltip: This is the diameter of your extruder nozzle (for example: 0.5, 0.35 etc.)

nozzle_width_warning_min.label: Width warning min
nozzle_width_warning_min.tooltip: Warn while editing when a configured extrusion width falls below this percentage of the nozzle diameter. Generated beads such as gap fill and thin walls are narrower by design and are not checked.

nozzle_width_warning_max.label: Width warning max
nozzle_width_warning_max.tooltip: Warn when an extrusion width exceeds this percentage of the nozzle diameter: configured values are checked while editing, and generated wall and fill widths are checked as they are produced while slicing. Support, skirt, brim and wipe tower widths are not checked. Set it to the widest bead the nozzle can properly iron down. Interlocking perimeters are exempt: their wide bonding beads are intentional.

host_type.label: Host Type
host_type.tooltip: Slic3r can upload G-code files to a printer host. This field must contain the kind of the host.

only_retract_when_crossing_perimeters.label: Only retract when crossing perimeters
only_retract_when_crossing_perimeters.tooltip: Disables retraction when the travel path does not exceed the upper layer's perimeters (and thus any ooze will be probably invisible).

ooze_prevention.label: Enable
ooze_prevention.tooltip: This option will drop the temperature of the inactive extruders to prevent oozing.

output_filename_format.label: Output filename format
output_filename_format.tooltip: You can use all configuration options as variables inside this template. For example: [layer_height], [fill_density] etc. You can also use [timestamp], [year], [month], [day], [hour], [minute], [second], [version], [input_filename_base], [default_output_extension].

overhangs.label: Detect bridging perimeters
overhangs.tooltip: Experimental option to adjust flow for overhangs (bridge flow will be used), to apply bridge speed to them and enable fan.

parking_pos_retraction.label: Filament parking position
parking_pos_retraction.tooltip: Distance of the extruder tip from the position where the filament is parked when unloaded. This should match the value in printer firmware.

extra_loading_move.label: Extra loading distance
extra_loading_move.tooltip: When set to zero, the distance the filament is moved from parking position during load is exactly the same as it was moved back during unload. When positive, it is loaded further,  if negative, the loading move is shorter than unloading.

multimaterial_purging.label: Purging volume
multimaterial_purging.tooltip: Determines purging volume on the wipe tower. This can be modified in Filament Settings ('filament_purge_multiplier') or overridden using project-specific settings.

perimeter_acceleration.label: Perimeters
perimeter_acceleration.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for perimeters. Set zero to disable acceleration control for perimeters.

external_perimeter_acceleration.label: External perimeters
external_perimeter_acceleration.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for external perimeters. Set zero to use the value for perimeters.

perimeter_extruder.label: Perimeter extruder
perimeter_extruder.tooltip: The extruder to use when printing perimeters and brim. First extruder is 1.

perimeter_extrusion_width.label: Perimeters
perimeter_extrusion_width.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for perimeters. You may want to use thinner extrudates to get more accurate surfaces. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise 1.125 x nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 200%) it will be computed over nozzle diameter or layer height, depending on the 'Percentages relative to nozzle size' setting.

perimeter_speed.label: Perimeters
perimeter_speed.tooltip: Speed for perimeters (contours, aka vertical shells). Set to zero for auto.

perimeters.label: Perimeters
perimeters.tooltip: This option sets the minimum number of perimeters to generate for each layer. preFlight may add extra perimeter loops in areas where the wall is wider than a single perimeter loop but too narrow for infill. The Extra Perimeters option can also increase this number on sloping surfaces.

serpentine_enabled.label: Enable Serpentine
serpentine_enabled.tooltip:
Prints a region as a continuous serpentine extrusion: a single line that weaves back and forth, inward from the walls. Without a depth limit it fills the whole cross-section, replacing the region's perimeters and infill; with a depth limit it forms a band along the walls and the interior is filled with normal infill.

Enabling this switches the perimeter generator to Athena and takes over the region's perimeters and most related wall settings.

Best on simple, symmetric parts such as nuts, bolts, and knurled knobs; complex shapes may slice poorly.

serpentine_extrusion_width.label: Serpentine extrusion width
serpentine_extrusion_width.tooltip: Width of the serpentine extrusion. If expressed as percentage (for example 105%), it will be computed over layer height. Set to 0 to use the external perimeter extrusion width.

serpentine_overlap.label: Serpentine overlap
serpentine_overlap.tooltip:
How deeply neighboring serpentine beads bond into each other. Percent values are computed over layer height, matching the Interlocking overlap semantics. Negative values spread the beads apart instead, leaving a uniform gap between them that lowers the effective density.

Default: 10.73% (safe starting point)

serpentine_max_bead.label: Serpentine maximum bead width
serpentine_max_bead.tooltip: Upper limit for bead widening, as a percent of the nozzle diameter. Where the pattern opens up at depth, beads grow up to this width to fill the gap.

serpentine_relaxed.label: Relaxed spacing
serpentine_relaxed.tooltip:
Space the serpentine teeth apart instead of packing them tightly: the bead follows the wall cleanly for the distance set below, then turns inward as a single solid rib and returns to the wall, like spokes on a wheel. The spacing acts as a fill density control while the part keeps one continuous bead and a single-bead wall.

Ribs stack vertically into continuous webs (the Ridges setting is ignored) and holes print as plain single-bead loops. The interior stays mostly open, so this suits open-top parts; solid top surfaces cannot bridge the cells. Overrides the depth limit when both are enabled.

serpentine_spacing.label: Rib spacing
serpentine_spacing.tooltip: Distance the bead follows the wall between ribs when Relaxed spacing is enabled. Ribs march from the seam at exactly this spacing in both directions; the leftover is absorbed by one wider or narrower cell on the far side, so rib columns stack into unbroken vertical webs even on tapered parts. Smaller values pack more ribs (denser fill); values below about two extrusion widths are floored to the classic dense pitch.

serpentine_outer_loop.label: Outer surface loop
serpentine_outer_loop.tooltip: Wraps one continuous perimeter around the outside of the serpentine pattern and moves the tooth-carrying wall just inside it, bonded to it. The tooth openings then interrupt only the hidden inner wall, so the outer surface is a single uninterrupted bead: the extrusion snakes out through one widened tooth, loops the whole object, and snakes back in, leaving a single seam-like crossover. The pattern stacks aligned so the seam forms one vertical column (the Ridges setting is ignored). Works at both classic and relaxed spacing.

serpentine_limit_depth.label: Limit Serpentine depth
serpentine_limit_depth.tooltip: Restrict the serpentine pattern to a wall of the depth set below instead of filling the whole region. The interior beyond that depth is filled normally (sparse infill, solid top and bottom layers), exactly like the leftover area behind ordinary perimeters. When disabled, the serpentine fills the entire region.

serpentine_depth.label: Serpentine depth
serpentine_depth.tooltip:
Maximum depth the serpentine wall reaches inward from the surface when "Limit Serpentine depth" is enabled. The interior beyond this depth is filled normally.

The smallest pattern that can close is two extrusion widths, so any smaller value is raised to that minimum.

serpentine_solid_surfaces.label: Solid top/bottom surfaces
serpentine_solid_surfaces.tooltip: Print the visible portions of top and bottom surfaces as ordinary solid infill, using the solid layer counts from Horizontal shells. The boundary keeps the serpentine zigzag at its shortest depth so the side pattern stays continuous, and covered interior areas continue as serpentine.

serpentine_ridges.label: Serpentine ridges
serpentine_ridges.tooltip:
Controls how the external zigzag ridges stack from layer to layer.
• Aligned: ridges stack vertically into straight columns.
• Staggered: the pattern staggers half a tooth each layer, so every cap is bridged by the layers above and below (brickwork).
• Random: the pattern lands at a random position on every layer.

serpentine_aim.label: Serpentine aim
serpentine_aim.tooltip: How depth-limited Serpentine teeth are aimed. Convergent points every tooth at the part center, giving a smooth radial fan (best for round parts like bolts and nuts). Perpendicular points each tooth square to the wall (best for curved or irregular parts). Only applies when depth limit is on.

interlock_perimeters_enabled.label: Enable interlocking perimeters
interlock_perimeters_enabled.tooltip: Creates interlocking layers by varying spacing of innermost perimeters across layers. When combined with over-extrusion, material compresses into gaps for enhanced layer bonding. Expected strength increase: 10-15% with no additional material or time cost.

interlock_perimeter_count.label: Interlocking perimeter count
interlock_perimeter_count.tooltip: Number of interlocking perimeter shells at sparse infill boundaries. These shells alternate overlap patterns between layers - each layer creates gaps that the next layer fills, forming mechanical interlocking.

interlock_regular_perimeters.label: Perimeters while interlocking
interlock_regular_perimeters.tooltip:
Overrides the number of regular perimeters on layers where interlocking is active. Layers near top/bottom surfaces (controlled by the solid layers settings) use the normal perimeter count.

0 = use the normal Perimeters setting (no override)
>0 = use this many regular perimeters on interlocking layers

This allows thinner walls on interior layers while retaining interlocking strength.

interlock_solid_layers_top.label: Above
interlock_solid_layers_top.tooltip: Number of solid layers between interlocking perimeters and a top surface. Ensures the interlocking pattern is fully hidden inside the object.

interlock_solid_layers_bottom.label: Below
interlock_solid_layers_bottom.tooltip: Number of solid layers between interlocking perimeters and a bottom surface. Ensures the interlocking pattern is fully hidden inside the object.

interlock_perimeter_strength.label: Interlocking strength
interlock_perimeter_strength.tooltip:
Controls interlocking extrusion amount. At 100%, inner interlocking shells extrude at 200% flow to compress material into gaps from the layer below.

100% = base interlocking (200% flow on inner shells)
150% = aggressive (may cause artifacts)

Note: The gap between interlocking shells is controlled separately by 'Interlocking overlap'.

interlock_perimeter_overlap.label: Interlocking overlap
interlock_perimeter_overlap.tooltip:
Controls the gap width between interlocking shells. Higher values narrow the channels and compress more material into the interlocking pattern, resulting in a stronger bond.

Default: 10.73% (safe starting point)

Start with a test print at 10.73% and increase gradually until over-extrusion is reached, then dial it back to the last safe value.

interlocking_perimeter_extruder.label: Interlocking perimeter extruder
interlocking_perimeter_extruder.tooltip: The extruder to use when printing interlocking perimeters. First extruder is 1.

interlock_flow_detection.label: Interlocking flow detection
interlock_flow_detection.tooltip:
Controls how precisely interlocking flow boundaries are detected. When interlocking perimeters cross from over-interlocking to non-interlocking regions, the flow rate must change. This setting determines how frequently boundaries are checked.

• Precise (1mm): Highest accuracy, checks every 1mm. Best quality at boundaries.
• Standard (2mm): Good balance of accuracy and speed.
• Relaxed (4mm): Faster slicing, minor boundary imprecision.
• Minimal (8mm): Fastest slicing, noticeable imprecision at boundaries.

Lower values increase slicing time but improve flow accuracy at zone boundaries.

post_process.label: Post-processing scripts
post_process.tooltip: If you want to process the output G-code through custom scripts, just list their absolute paths here. Separate multiple scripts with a semicolon.
