Scripts will be passed the absolute path to the G-code file as the first argument, and they can access the Slic3r config settings by reading environment variables.

export_script_enabled.label: Enable export script
export_script_enabled.tooltip: When enabled, an 'Export to Script' option appears in the export menu. The configured Python script receives the G-code data and handles output - saving to disk, uploading via FTP, or both.

export_script.label: Export script
export_script.tooltip: Path to a Python script that handles G-code export. The script must define an export(gcode) function that receives a gcode object with .data (list of G-code lines) and .filename (suggested output name).

preprocessing_enabled_filament.label: Enable preprocessing
preprocessing_enabled_filament.tooltip: Enable Python preprocessing scripts for this filament profile. Scripts run during slicing and can read/modify G-code moves.

preprocessing_enabled_print.label: Enable preprocessing
preprocessing_enabled_print.tooltip: Enable Python preprocessing scripts for this print profile. Scripts run during slicing and can read/modify G-code moves.

preprocessing_enabled_printer.label: Enable preprocessing
preprocessing_enabled_printer.tooltip: Enable Python preprocessing scripts for this printer profile. Scripts run during slicing and can read/modify G-code moves.

preprocessing_scripts_filament.label: Preprocessing scripts
preprocessing_scripts_filament.tooltip: Ordered list of Python preprocessing script paths for this filament profile.

preprocessing_scripts_print.label: Preprocessing scripts
preprocessing_scripts_print.tooltip: Ordered list of Python preprocessing script paths for this print profile.

preprocessing_scripts_printer.label: Preprocessing scripts
preprocessing_scripts_printer.tooltip: Ordered list of Python preprocessing script paths for this printer profile.

printer_notes.label: Printer notes
printer_notes.tooltip: You can put your notes regarding the printer here.

printer_variant.label: Printer variant
printer_variant.tooltip: Name of the printer variant. For example, the printer variants may be differentiated by a nozzle diameter.

raft_contact_distance.label: Raft contact Z distance
raft_contact_distance.tooltip: The vertical distance between object and raft. Ignored for soluble interface.

raft_expansion.label: Raft expansion
raft_expansion.tooltip: Expansion of the raft in XY plane for better stability.

raft_first_layer_density.label: First layer density
raft_first_layer_density.tooltip: Density of the first raft or support layer.

raft_first_layer_expansion.label: First layer expansion
raft_first_layer_expansion.tooltip: Expansion of the first raft or support layer to improve adhesion to print bed.

raft_layers.label: Raft layers
raft_layers.tooltip: The object will be raised by this number of layers, and support material will be generated under it.

resolution.label: Slice resolution
resolution.tooltip: Minimum detail resolution, used to simplify the input file for speeding up the slicing job and reducing memory usage. High-resolution models often carry more detail than printers can render. Set to zero to disable any simplification and use full resolution from input.

gcode_resolution.label: G-code resolution
gcode_resolution.tooltip: Maximum deviation of exported G-code paths from their full resolution counterparts. Very high resolution G-code requires huge amount of RAM to slice and preview, also a 3D printer may stutter not being able to process a high resolution G-code in a timely manner. On the other hand, a low resolution G-code will produce a low poly effect and because the G-code reduction is performed at each layer independently, visible artifacts may be produced.

retract_before_travel.label: Minimum travel after retraction
retract_before_travel.tooltip: Retraction is not triggered when travel moves are shorter than this length.

retract_before_wipe.label: Retract amount before wipe
retract_before_wipe.tooltip: With bowden extruders, it may be wise to do some amount of quick retract before doing the wipe movement.

wipe_extend.label: Extend wipe
wipe_extend.tooltip: When enabled, the wipe move continues in the same direction as the last extrusion move. When disabled (default), the wipe follows the perimeter loop for the duration of the move.

wipe_length.label: Wipe length
wipe_length.tooltip: Length of the wipe move. When using firmware retraction or without 'Wipe while retracting', the wipe will be a pure travel move (no retraction). Set to 0 to use the default wipe behavior based on retraction length.

retract_layer_change.label: Retract on layer change
retract_layer_change.tooltip: This flag enforces a retraction whenever a Z move is done.

retract_length.label: Retraction length
retract_length.tooltip: When retraction is triggered, filament is pulled back by the specified amount (the length is measured on raw filament, before it enters the extruder).

retract_length_toolchange.label: Length
retract_length_toolchange.tooltip: When retraction is triggered before changing tool, filament is pulled back by the specified amount (the length is measured on raw filament, before it enters the extruder).

travel_slope.label: Ramping slope angle
travel_slope.tooltip: Slope of the ramp in the initial phase of the travel.

travel_ramping_lift.label: Use ramping lift
travel_ramping_lift.tooltip: Generates a ramping lift instead of lifting the extruder directly upwards. The travel is split into two phases: the ramp and the standard horizontal travel. This option helps reduce stringing.

travel_max_lift.label: Maximum ramping lift
travel_max_lift.tooltip: Maximum lift height of the ramping lift. It may not be reached if the next position is close to the old one.

travel_lift_before_obstacle.label: Steeper ramp before obstacles
travel_lift_before_obstacle.tooltip: If enabled, preFlight detects obstacles along the travel path and makes the slope steeper in case an obstacle might be hit during the initial phase of the travel.

nozzle_high_flow.label: High flow nozzle
nozzle_high_flow.tooltip:
High flow nozzles allow higher print speeds.

Note: This value is controlled from Print Settings > Advanced > Tool Configuration

retract_lift_above.label: Above Z
retract_lift_above.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place above the specified absolute Z. You can tune this setting for skipping lift on the first layers.

retract_lift_below.label: Below Z
retract_lift_below.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place below the specified absolute Z. You can tune this setting for limiting lift to the first layers.

retract_restart_extra.label: Deretraction extra length
retract_restart_extra.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after the travel move, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament. This setting is rarely needed.

retract_restart_extra_toolchange.label: Extra length on restart
retract_restart_extra_toolchange.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after changing tool, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament.

retract_speed.label: Retraction Speed
retract_speed.tooltip: The speed for retractions (it only applies to the extruder motor).

deretract_speed.label: Deretraction Speed
deretract_speed.tooltip: The speed for loading of a filament into extruder after retraction (it only applies to the extruder motor). If left to zero, the retraction speed is used.

seam_gap_distance.label: Seam gap distance
seam_gap_distance.tooltip: The distance between the endpoints of a closed loop perimeter. Positive values will shorten and interrupt the loop slightly to reduce the seam. Negative values will extend the loop, causing the endpoints to overlap slightly. When percents are used, the distance is derived from the nozzle diameter. Set to zero to disable this feature.

staggered_inner_seams.label: Staggered inner seams
staggered_inner_seams.tooltip: This option causes the inner seams to be shifted backwards based on their depth, forming a zigzag pattern.

seam_type.label: Seam type
seam_type.tooltip:
Controls how the seam point on external perimeters is shaped to hide start/stop blobs.

Regular - No seam shaping. Standard seam behavior.

Nip/Tuck - Creates a V-shaped channel one perimeter deep at the seam. Both the start and end of the external perimeter are pushed inward, and the first inner perimeter is trimmed to absorb the disturbance.

Nip - Only the start of the external perimeter is pushed inward at the seam. The end remains on the normal path. The inner perimeter is trimmed on the start side only.

Tuck - Only the end of the external perimeter is pushed inward at the seam. The start remains on the normal path. The inner perimeter is trimmed on the end side only.

Alt. Nip/Tuck - Alternates between Nip on even layers and Tuck on odd layers. This distributes the seam disturbance across both sides of the junction, preventing a consistent bulge on one side.

Note: All non-Regular modes require multiple perimeters and are not used in Spiral Vase mode.

seam_notch_width.label: Seam notch width
seam_notch_width.tooltip: Width of the V-shaped notch as a multiple of the external perimeter extrusion width. In Nip/Tuck mode, this is the full notch width across both sides of the seam. In Nip or Tuck mode, only half the width is used since only one side of the seam is shaped. The depth is automatically calculated from perimeter spacing. Wider values are more forgiving for blobs but create a larger surface depression. Narrower values are subtler.

seam_notch_angle.label: Seam notch corner threshold
seam_notch_angle.tooltip:
Controls where seam notching is applied based on corner sharpness. At sharp corners the seam is naturally hidden by the geometry, so notching is unnecessary.

Seams on corners sharper than this angle are skipped. The default of 44° means any corner of 44° or less is considered sharp enough to hide the seam on its own - just under 45°, where a clean fold already conceals the junction.

Set to 0 to apply seam notching everywhere regardless of corner angle.

scarf_seam_placement.label: Scarf joint placement
scarf_seam_placement.tooltip: Where to place scarf joint seam.

scarf_seam_only_on_smooth.label: Scarf joint only on smooth perimeters
scarf_seam_only_on_smooth.fullLabel: Scarf joint only on smooth perimeters
scarf_seam_only_on_smooth.tooltip: Only use the scarf joint when the perimeter is smooth.

scarf_seam_start_height.label: Scarf start height
scarf_seam_start_height.tooltip: Start height of the scarf joint specified as fraction of the current layer height.

scarf_seam_entire_loop.label: Scarf joint around entire perimeter
scarf_seam_entire_loop.tooltip: Extend the scarf around entire length of the perimeter.

scarf_seam_max_segment_length.label: Max scarf joint segment length
scarf_seam_max_segment_length.tooltip: Maximum length of any scarf joint segment.

scarf_seam_on_inner_perimeters.label: Scarf joint on inner perimeters
scarf_seam_on_inner_perimeters.tooltip: Use scarf joint on inner perimeters.

seam_preferred_direction_jitter.label: Jitter
seam_preferred_direction_jitter.tooltip: Preferred direction of the seam - jitter

skirt_distance.label: Distance from brim/object
skirt_distance.tooltip: Distance between skirt and brim (when draft shield is not used) or objects.

skirt_height.label: Skirt height
skirt_height.tooltip: Height of skirt expressed in layers.

draft_shield.label: Draft shield
draft_shield.tooltip:
With draft shield active, the skirt will be printed skirt_distance from the object, possibly intersecting brim.
Enabled = skirt is as tall as the highest printed object.
Limited = skirt is as tall as specified by skirt_height.
This is useful to protect an ABS or ASA print from warping and detaching from print bed due to wind draft.

skirts.label: Loops (minimum)
skirts.tooltip: Number of loops for the skirt. If the Minimum Extrusion Length option is set, the number of loops might be greater than the one configured here. Set this to zero to disable skirt completely.

slowdown_below_layer_time.label: Slow down if layer print time is below
slowdown_below_layer_time.fullLabel: Slow down if layer print time is below
slowdown_below_layer_time.tooltip: If layer print time is estimated below this number of seconds, print moves speed will be scaled down to extend duration to this value.

dont_slow_down_outer_wall.label: Don't slow down outer walls
dont_slow_down_outer_wall.tooltip: If enabled, outer wall speed will not be reduced to meet the minimum layer time. This prevents wall thickness variation on thin-walled parts where the cooling slowdown would otherwise cause over-extrusion at reduced speeds.

small_perimeter_speed.label: Small perimeters
small_perimeter_speed.tooltip: Speed for perimeters having radius <= 6.5mm (usually holes). A percentage is recommended - it will be calculated as a percentage of the perimeter speed, whether set manually or calculated by auto speed. Set to zero to use the full perimeter speed.

solid_infill_below_area.label: Solid infill threshold area
solid_infill_below_area.tooltip: Force solid infill for regions having a smaller area than the specified threshold.

solid_infill_extruder.label: Solid infill extruder
solid_infill_extruder.tooltip: The extruder to use when printing solid infill.

solid_infill_every_layers.label: Solid infill every
solid_infill_every_layers.tooltip: This feature allows to force a solid layer every given number of layers. Zero to disable. You can set this to any value (for example 9999); Slic3r will automatically choose the maximum possible number of layers to combine according to nozzle diameter and layer height.

solid_infill_extrusion_width.label: Solid infill
solid_infill_extrusion_width.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for infill for solid surfaces. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise 1.125 x nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over nozzle diameter or layer height, depending on the 'Percentages relative to nozzle size' setting.

solid_infill_speed.label: Solid infill
solid_infill_speed.tooltip: Speed for printing solid regions (top/bottom/internal horizontal shells). This can be expressed as a percentage (for example: 80%) over the default infill speed above. Set to zero for auto.

solid_layers.label: Solid layers
solid_layers.tooltip: Number of solid layers to generate on top and bottom surfaces.

solid_min_thickness.label: Minimum thickness of a top / bottom shell
solid_min_thickness.fullLabel: Minimum thickness of a top / bottom shell
solid_min_thickness.tooltip: Minimum thickness of a top / bottom shell

spiral_vase.label: Spiral vase
spiral_vase.tooltip: This feature will raise Z gradually while printing a single-walled object in order to remove any visible seam. This option requires a single perimeter, no infill, no top solid layers and no support material. You can still set any number of bottom solid layers as well as skirt/brim loops. It won't work when printing more than one single object.

standby_temperature_delta.label: Temperature variation
standby_temperature_delta.tooltip: Temperature difference to be applied when an extruder is not active. The value is not used when 'idle_temperature' in filament settings is defined.

autoemit_temperature_commands.label: Emit temperature commands automatically
autoemit_temperature_commands.tooltip:
When enabled, preFlight will check whether your custom Start G-Code contains G-codes to set extruder, bed or chamber temperature (M104, M109, M140, M190, M141 and M191). If so, the temperatures will not be emitted automatically so you're free to customize the order of heating commands and other custom actions. Note that you can use placeholder variables for all preFlight settings, so you can put a "M109 S[first_layer_temperature]" command wherever you want.
If your custom Start G-Code does NOT contain these G-codes, preFlight will execute the Start G-Code after heated chamber was set to its temperature, bed reached its target temperature and extruder just started heating.

When disabled, preFlight will NOT emit commands to heat up extruder, bed or chamber, leaving all to Custom Start G-Code.

start_gcode.label: Start G-code
start_gcode.tooltip: This start procedure is inserted at the beginning, possibly prepended by temperature-changing commands. See 'autoemit_temperature_commands'.

start_filament_gcode.label: Start G-code
start_filament_gcode.tooltip: This start procedure is inserted at the beginning, after any printer start gcode (and after any toolchange to this filament in case of multi-material printers). This is used to override settings for a specific filament. If preFlight detects M104, M109, M140 or M190 in your custom codes, such commands will not be prepended automatically so you're free to customize the order of heating commands and other custom actions. Note that you can use placeholder variables for all preFlight settings, so you can put a "M109 S[first_layer_temperature]" command wherever you want. If you have multiple extruders, the gcode is processed in extruder order.

color_change_gcode.label: Color change G-code
color_change_gcode.tooltip: This G-code will be used as a code for the color change

pause_print_gcode.label: Pause Print G-code
pause_print_gcode.tooltip: This G-code will be used as a code for the pause print

template_custom_gcode.label: Custom G-code
template_custom_gcode.tooltip: This G-code will be used as a custom code

single_extruder_multi_material.label: Single Extruder Multi Material
single_extruder_multi_material.tooltip: The printer multiplexes filaments into a single hot end.

single_extruder_multi_material_priming.label: Prime all printing extruders
single_extruder_multi_material_priming.tooltip: If enabled, all printing extruders will be primed at the front edge of the print bed at the start of the print.

wipe_tower_no_sparse_layers.label: No sparse layers (EXPERIMENTAL)
wipe_tower_no_sparse_layers.tooltip: If enabled, the wipe tower will not be printed on layers with no toolchanges. On layers with a toolchange, extruder will travel downward to print the wipe tower. User is responsible for ensuring there is no collision with the print.

slice_closing_radius.label: Slice gap closing radius
slice_closing_radius.tooltip: Cracks smaller than 2x gap closing radius are being filled during the triangle mesh slicing. The gap closing operation may reduce the final print resolution, therefore it is advisable to keep the value reasonably low.

slicing_mode.label: Slicing Mode
slicing_mode.tooltip: Use "Even-odd" for 3DLabPrint airplane models. Use "Close holes" to close all holes in the model.

support_material_auto.label: Auto generated supports
support_material_auto.tooltip: If checked, supports will be generated automatically based on the overhang threshold value. If unchecked, supports will be generated inside the "Support Enforcer" volumes only.

support_material_xy_spacing.label: XY separation between an object and its support
support_material_xy_spacing.fullLabel: XY separation between an object and its support
support_material_xy_spacing.tooltip: XY separation between an object and its support. If expressed as percentage (for example 50%), it will be calculated over external perimeter width.

support_material_angle.label: Pattern angle
support_material_angle.tooltip: Use this setting to rotate the support material pattern on the horizontal plane.

support_material_buildplate_only.label: Support on build plate only
support_material_buildplate_only.tooltip: Only create auto-detected support if it lies on a build plate. Don't create support on a print. This setting only applies when auto-generated supports are enabled; painted supports are always placed exactly where painted.

support_material_contact_distance.label: Top contact Z distance
support_material_contact_distance.tooltip:
The vertical distance between object and support material interface. Setting this to No gap will also prevent preFlight from using bridge flow and speed for the first object layer.

Without interface layers, only No gap or Full layer height are effective. Half layer and Custom values require interface layers for precise gap control.

support_material_contact_distance_custom.label: Custom top contact gap
support_material_contact_distance_custom.tooltip: Custom vertical distance between object and support material interface. Only used when Top contact Z distance is set to Custom. The gap is achieved by adjusting interface layer heights. With very few interface layers (0-1), the exact gap may be approximated.

support_material_top_contact_extrusion_w.label: Top contact extrusion width
support_material_top_contact_extrusion_w.tooltip:
Width of extrusions for the top support interface layer, as a percentage of the interface width. Lower values create thinner extrusions for easier separation from the supported surface. 100% uses the full interface width.

The actual width will never go below the layer height to prevent extrusion errors.

Without interface layers, this setting only applies when Top contact Z distance is set to 0 (no gap).

support_material_bottom_contact_distance.label: Bottom contact Z distance
support_material_bottom_contact_distance.tooltip: The vertical distance between the object top surface and the support material interface. Options are relative to layer height to ensure proper alignment when supports merge.

support_material_bottom_contact_extrusio.label: Bottom contact extrusion width
support_material_bottom_contact_extrusio.tooltip:
Width of extrusions for the bottom contact layer when using half-layer gap, as a percentage of the interface width. Lower values create a larger gap for easier support removal. Height is always 50% of layer height; this controls the width.

The actual width will never go below the extrusion height to prevent extrusion errors.

support_material_enforce_layers.label: Enforce support for the first
support_material_enforce_layers.fullLabel: Enforce support for the first n layers
support_material_enforce_layers.tooltip: Generate support material for the specified number of layers counting from bottom, regardless of whether normal support material is enabled or not and regardless of any angle threshold. This is useful for getting more adhesion of objects having a very thin or poor footprint on the build plate.

support_material_extruder.label: Support material extruder
support_material_extruder.tooltip: The extruder to use when printing support material, raft and skirt (1+, 0 to use the current extruder to minimize tool changes).

support_material_extrusion_width.label: Support material
support_material_extrusion_width.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for support material. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over nozzle diameter or layer height, depending on the 'Percentages relative to nozzle size' setting.

support_material_interface_extrusion_wid.label: Support material interface
support_material_interface_extrusion_wid.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for support interface layers. If left zero, the Support material extrusion width will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over nozzle diameter or layer height, depending on the 'Percentages relative to nozzle size' setting.

support_material_interface_contact_loops.label: Interface loops
support_material_interface_contact_loops.tooltip: Cover the top contact layer of the supports with loops. Disabled by default.

support_material_interface_extruder.label: Support material interface extruder
support_material_interface_extruder.tooltip: The extruder to use when printing support material interface (1+, 0 to use the current extruder to minimize tool changes). This affects raft too.

support_material_interface_layers.label: Top interface layers
support_material_interface_layers.tooltip: Number of solid interface layers between the support structure and the object. These layers distribute the gap specified in 'Top contact Z distance' - more layers allow finer gap control. With fewer layers, the exact gap may not be achievable and will be approximated within safe extrusion limits (25-75% of nozzle diameter per layer).

support_material_bottom_interface_layers.label: Bottom interface layers
support_material_bottom_interface_layers.tooltip: Number of interface layers to insert between the object(s) and support material. Set to -1 to use the same value as 'Top interface layers'.

support_material_closing_radius.label: Closing radius
support_material_closing_radius.tooltip: For snug supports, the support regions will be merged using morphological closing operation. Gaps smaller than the closing radius will be filled in.

support_material_min_area.label: Minimum support area
support_material_min_area.tooltip:
Paint-on support regions smaller than this area will be filtered out. This prevents accidental tiny paint specs from generating support structures.

Reference - circle diameter to area:
• 0.5mm diameter = 0.2 mm²
• 1.0mm diameter = 0.79 mm²
• 1.5mm diameter = 1.77 mm²
• 2.0mm diameter = 3.14 mm²

Set to 0 to disable filtering.

support_material_interface_spacing.label: Interface pattern spacing
support_material_interface_spacing.tooltip: Spacing between interface lines. Set zero to get a solid interface.

support_material_interface_speed.label: Support material interface
support_material_interface_speed.tooltip: Speed for printing support material interface layers. If expressed as percentage (for example 50%) it will be calculated over support material speed.

support_material_pattern.label: Pattern
support_material_pattern.tooltip: Pattern used to generate support material.

support_material_bridge_no_gap.label: Bridge fill when "no gap" selected
support_material_bridge_no_gap.tooltip:
When enabled, bottom surfaces use bridge infill instead of solid infill when support contact distance is set to "no gap". Bridge infill uses slower speeds and flow rates optimized for printing over air.

When disabled (default), all bottom surfaces use solid infill when "no gap" is selected, since the support provides a stable printing surface.

Note: This applies to all bottom surfaces, not just areas with support underneath.

support_material_interface_pattern.label: Interface pattern
support_material_interface_pattern.tooltip: Pattern used to generate support material interface. Default pattern for non-soluble support interface is Rectilinear, while default pattern for soluble support interface is Concentric.

support_material_style.label: Style
support_material_style.tooltip: Style and shape of the support towers for auto-generated supports. Projecting the supports into a regular grid will create more stable supports, while snug support towers will save material and reduce object scarring. Note: This setting only affects auto-generated supports. Paint-on supports specify their own type (Blocker/Snug/Grid/Organic/Baobab) and will override this setting in painted regions.

support_material_synchronize_layers.label: Synchronize with object layers
support_material_synchronize_layers.tooltip: Synchronize support layers with the object print layers. This is useful with multi-material printers, where the extruder switch is expensive. This option is only available when top contact Z distance is set to zero.

support_material_threshold.label: Overhang threshold
support_material_threshold.tooltip: Support material will not be generated for overhangs whose slope angle (90° = vertical) is above the given threshold. In other words, this value represent the most horizontal slope (measured from the horizontal plane) that you can print without support material. Set to zero for automatic detection (recommended).

support_material_with_sheath.label: With sheath around the support
support_material_with_sheath.tooltip: Add a sheath (a single perimeter line) around the base support. This makes the support more reliable, but also more difficult to remove.

support_baobab_angle.label: Maximum trunk angle
support_baobab_angle.tooltip: The maximum angle of the trunks, from vertical, when they have to avoid the model. Use a lower angle to make them more vertical and more stable. Use a higher angle to be able to have more reach.

support_baobab_angle_slow.label: Preferred trunk angle
support_baobab_angle_slow.tooltip: The preferred angle of the trunks when they do not have to avoid the model. Use a lower angle to make them more vertical and more stable. Use a higher angle for trunks to merge faster.

support_baobab_canopy_density.label: Canopy density
support_baobab_canopy_density.tooltip: Density of the lightning fill inside a Baobab support's canopy. The fill carries the support interface across the canopy's mouth. A higher value gives the interface more to land on but uses more material and time.

support_baobab_max_canopy_angle.label: Maximum canopy angle
support_baobab_max_canopy_angle.tooltip: The maximum angle, from vertical, at which a Baobab support's canopy tapers down onto its trunk. A higher angle reaches the trunk sooner and makes a shallower canopy. It is reduced automatically where a layer would grow outward by more than half the support extrusion width, and where a leaning trunk already spends part of that allowance.

support_baobab_plant_on_model.label: Plant trunks on object
support_baobab_plant_on_model.tooltip: Allow trunks to land on stable top surfaces of the object instead of always descending to the build plate. A surface qualifies when it is wide enough for the whole foot and backed by solid material beneath it.

support_baobab_trunk_diameter.label: Trunk diameter
support_baobab_trunk_diameter.tooltip: The diameter of the thinnest trunks. Thicker trunks are more sturdy. Trunks towards the base will be thicker than this.

support_baobab_trunk_diameter_angle.label: Trunk diameter angle
support_baobab_trunk_diameter_angle.tooltip: The angle of the trunks' diameter as they gradually become thicker towards the bottom. An angle of 0 will cause the trunks to have uniform thickness over their length. A bit of an angle can increase stability.

support_baobab_trunk_distance.label: Trunk distance
support_baobab_trunk_distance.tooltip: How much interface area a single trunk gathers: seeds closer than this distance share a trunk, and each canopy reaches this far from its trunk to cover its share of the interface.

support_tree_angle.label: Maximum branch angle
support_tree_angle.tooltip: The maximum angle of the branches, when the branches have to avoid the model. Use a lower angle to make them more vertical and more stable. Use a higher angle to be able to have more reach.

support_tree_angle_slow.label: Preferred branch angle
support_tree_angle_slow.tooltip: The preferred angle of the branches, when they do not have to avoid the model. Use a lower angle to make them more vertical and more stable. Use a higher angle for branches to merge faster.

support_tree_tip_diameter.label: Tip diameter
support_tree_tip_diameter.tooltip: Branch tip diameter for organic supports.

support_tree_branch_diameter.label: Branch diameter
support_tree_branch_diameter.tooltip: The diameter of the thinnest branches of organic support. Thicker branches are more sturdy. Branches towards the base will be thicker than this.

support_tree_branch_diameter_angle.label: Branch diameter angle
support_tree_branch_diameter_angle.tooltip: The angle of the branches' diameter as they gradually become thicker towards the bottom. An angle of 0 will cause the branches to have uniform thickness over their length. A bit of an angle can increase stability of the organic support.

support_tree_branch_diameter_double_wall.label: Branch diameter with double walls
support_tree_branch_diameter_double_wall.tooltip: Branches with area larger than the area of a circle of this diameter will be printed with double walls for stability. Set this value to zero for no double walls.

support_tree_branch_distance.label: Branch distance
support_tree_branch_distance.tooltip: How far apart the branches need to be when they touch the model. Making this distance small will cause the tree support to touch the model at more points, causing better overhang but making support harder to remove.

support_tree_top_rate.label: Branch density
support_tree_top_rate.tooltip: Adjusts the density of the support structure used to generate the tips of the branches. A higher value results in better overhangs but the supports are harder to remove, thus it is recommended to enable top support interfaces instead of a high branch density value if dense interfaces are needed.

temperature.label: Other layers
temperature.tooltip: Nozzle temperature for layers after the first one. Set this to zero to keep the first layer nozzle temperature for the entire print.

thick_bridges.label: Thick bridges
thick_bridges.tooltip: Deprecated: This setting is disabled in preFlight. Thick bridges interfere with support interface gap calculations.

thin_walls.label: Detect thin walls
thin_walls.tooltip: Detect single-width walls (parts where two extrusions don't fit and we need to collapse them into a single trace).

toolchange_gcode.label: Tool change G-code
toolchange_gcode.tooltip: This custom code is inserted before every toolchange. Placeholder variables for all preFlight settings as well as {toolchange_z}, {previous_extruder} and {next_extruder} can be used. When a tool-changing command which changes to the correct extruder is included (such as T{next_extruder}), preFlight will emit no other such command. It is therefore possible to script custom behaviour both before and after the toolchange.

top_infill_extrusion_width.label: Top solid infill
top_infill_extrusion_width.tooltip: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for infill for top surfaces. You may want to use thinner extrudates to fill all narrow regions and get a smoother finish. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over nozzle diameter or layer height, depending on the 'Percentages relative to nozzle size' setting.

top_solid_infill_speed.label: Top solid infill
top_solid_infill_speed.tooltip: Speed for printing top solid layers (it only applies to the uppermost external layers and not to their internal solid layers). You may want to slow down this to get a nicer surface finish. This can be expressed as a percentage (for example: 80%) over the solid infill speed above. Set to zero for auto.

top_solid_layers.label: TopLayers
top_solid_layers.tooltip: Number of solid layers to generate on top surfaces.

top_solid_min_thickness.label: TopLayers
top_solid_min_thickness.tooltip: The number of top solid layers is increased above top_solid_layers if necessary to satisfy minimum thickness of top shell. This is useful to prevent pillowing effect when printing with variable layer height.

top_surface_flow_reduction.label: Top surface flow reduction
top_surface_flow_reduction.tooltip: Reduces extrusion flow for visible top surfaces (perimeters and solid infill). This helps prevent overextrusion artifacts on visible surfaces. The percentage is subtracted from 100% (e.g., 3% means 97% flow). Set to 0% to disable. Top solid infill always uses reduced flow when enabled; perimeters use visibility detection to only reduce flow on truly visible segments.

top_surface_visibility_detection.label: Visibility detection
top_surface_visibility_detection.tooltip:
Controls how precisely the boundary between visible and hidden perimeter segments is detected. Higher precision means more accurate boundaries but slower slicing.

• Precise (1mm): Highest accuracy, samples every 1mm along perimeters
• Standard (2mm): Good balance of accuracy and speed (recommended)
• Relaxed (4mm): Faster slicing with slightly less precise boundaries
• Minimal (8mm): Fastest, may miss some visibility transitions

merge_top_solid_infills.label: Merge top solid infills
merge_top_solid_infills.tooltip: When enabled, top solid infills will be merged with adjacent internal solid infills to improve print efficiency. WARNING: On certain objects, this feature may incorrectly convert solid infill into top solid infill, or cause slight misalignment of top surface patterns. Disable if precise top surface alignment is critical.

narrow_to_athena.label: Narrow to Athena
narrow_to_athena.tooltip: Replace zigzag patterns in narrow solid infill areas with Athena variable-width fill. Athena generates clean adaptive-width paths that follow the contour of narrow regions without zigzags or tight loop artifacts. Areas narrower than the Narrow threshold will be converted. Applies to internal solid, top solid, and bottom solid infill. Does not affect bridge infill.

narrow_to_athena_threshold.label: Narrow threshold
narrow_to_athena_threshold.tooltip: Solid infill areas (internal, top, and bottom) narrower than this many extrusion widths will use Athena variable-width fill instead of the configured fill pattern. Only applies when 'Narrow to Athena' is enabled.

narrow_to_athena_top_bottom.label: Narrow to Athena on top/bottom
narrow_to_athena_top_bottom.tooltip: Also apply Narrow to Athena to top and bottom solid surfaces, not only internal solid. Thin areas of these visible surfaces convert to a smooth Athena bead instead of the configured pattern, while wider areas keep it. Only applies when 'Narrow to Athena' is enabled.

travel_speed.label: Travel
travel_speed.tooltip: Speed for travel moves (jumps between distant extrusion points).

travel_speed_z.label: Z travel
travel_speed_z.tooltip:
Speed for movements along the Z axis.
When set to zero, the value is ignored and regular travel speed is used instead.

use_firmware_retraction.label: Use firmware retraction
use_firmware_retraction.tooltip: This setting uses G10 and G11 commands to have the firmware handle the retraction. Note that this has to be supported by firmware.

use_relative_e_distances.label: Use relative E distances
use_relative_e_distances.tooltip: If your firmware requires relative E values, check this, otherwise leave it unchecked. Most firmwares use absolute values.

use_volumetric_e.label: Use volumetric E
use_volumetric_e.tooltip: This experimental setting uses outputs the E values in cubic millimeters instead of linear millimeters. If your firmware doesn't already know filament diameter(s), you can put commands like 'M200 D[filament_diameter_0] T0' in your start G-code in order to turn volumetric mode on and use the filament diameter associated to the filament selected in Slic3r. This is only supported in recent Marlin.

time_cost.label: Machine hourly rate
time_cost.tooltip: Hourly operating cost of this printer. Combined with filament cost to calculate total job cost.

currency_symbol.label: Currency symbol
currency_symbol.tooltip: Currency symbol displayed with cost estimates (e.g. $, EUR, GBP).

variable_layer_height.label: Enable variable layer height feature
variable_layer_height.tooltip: Some printers or printer setups may have difficulties printing with a variable layer height. Enabled by default.

prefer_clockwise_movements.label: Prefer clockwise movements
prefer_clockwise_movements.tooltip: This setting makes the printer print loops clockwise instead of counterclockwise.

wipe.label: Wipe while retracting
wipe.tooltip: This flag will move the nozzle while retracting to minimize the possible blob on leaky extruders.

wipe_tower.label: Enable
wipe_tower.tooltip: Multi material printers may need to prime or purge extruders on tool changes. Extrude the excess material into the wipe tower.

wiping_volumes_matrix.label: Purging volumes - matrix
wiping_volumes_matrix.tooltip: This matrix describes volumes (in cubic milimetres) required to purge the new filament on the wipe tower for any given pair of tools.

wipe_tower_cone_angle.label: Stabilization cone apex angle
wipe_tower_cone_angle.tooltip: Angle at the apex of the cone that is used to stabilize the wipe tower. Larger angle means wider base.

wipe_tower_extra_spacing.label: Wipe tower purge lines spacing
wipe_tower_extra_spacing.tooltip: Spacing of purge lines on the wipe tower.

wipe_tower_extra_flow.label: Extra flow for purging
wipe_tower_extra_flow.tooltip: Extra flow used for the purging lines on the wipe tower. This makes the purging lines thicker or narrower than they normally would be. The spacing is adjusted automatically.

wipe_into_infill.label: Wipe into this object's infill
wipe_into_infill.tooltip: Purging after toolchange will be done inside this object's infills. This lowers the amount of waste but may result in longer print time  due to additional travel moves.

wipe_into_objects.label: Wipe into this object
wipe_into_objects.tooltip: Object will be used to purge the nozzle after a toolchange to save material that would otherwise end up in the wipe tower and decrease print time. Colours of the objects will be mixed as a result.

wipe_tower_bridging.label: Maximal bridging distance
wipe_tower_bridging.tooltip: Maximal distance between supports on sparse infill sections.

wipe_tower_extruder.label: Wipe tower extruder
wipe_tower_extruder.tooltip: The extruder to use when printing perimeter of the wipe tower. Set to 0 to use the one that is available (non-soluble would be preferred).

xy_size_compensation.label: XY Size Compensation
xy_size_compensation.tooltip: The object will be grown/shrunk in the XY plane by the configured value (negative = inwards, positive = outwards). This might be useful for fine-tuning hole sizes.

z_offset.label: Z offset
z_offset.tooltip: This value will be added (or subtracted) from all the Z coordinates in the output G-code. It is used to compensate for bad Z endstop position: for example, if your endstop zero actually leaves the nozzle 0.3mm far from the print bed, set this to -0.3 (or fix your endstop).

perimeter_generator.label: Perimeter generator
perimeter_generator.tooltip: Athena (Precise) produces precise perimeters with exact user-specified widths for maximum dimensional accuracy. Arachne (Variable) produces perimeters with variable extrusion width for better handling of thin walls and complex details. This setting also affects the Concentric infill.

wall_transition_length.label: Perimeter transition length
wall_transition_length.tooltip: When transitioning between different numbers of perimeters as the part becomes thinner, a certain amount of space is allotted to split or join the perimeter segments. If expressed as a percentage (for example 100%), it will be computed based on the nozzle diameter.

wall_transition_filter_deviation.label: Perimeter transition filter margin
wall_transition_filter_deviation.tooltip: Prevent transitioning back and forth between one extra perimeter and one less. This margin extends the range of extrusion widths which follow to [Minimum perimeter width - margin, 2 * Minimum perimeter width + margin]. Increasing this margin reduces the number of transitions, which reduces the number of extrusion starts/stops and travel time. However, large extrusion width variation can lead to under- or overextrusion problems. If expressed as a percentage (for example 25%), it will be computed based on the nozzle diameter.

wall_transition_angle.label: Perimeter transition angle
wall_transition_angle.tooltip: When to create transitions between even and odd numbers of perimeters. A wedge shape with an angle greater than this setting will not have transitions and no perimeters will be printed in the center to fill the remaining space. Reducing this setting reduces the number and length of these center perimeters, but may leave gaps or overextrude.

wall_distribution_count.label: Perimeter distribution count
wall_distribution_count.tooltip: The number of perimeters, counted from the center, over which the variation needs to be spread. Lower values mean that the outer perimeters don't change in width.

min_feature_size.label: Minimum feature size
min_feature_size.tooltip: Minimum thickness of thin features. Model features thinner than this value are not generated. If expressed as a percentage (for example 25%), it will be computed based on the nozzle diameter.

min_bead_width.label: Minimum perimeter width
min_bead_width.tooltip: Width of the perimeter that will replace thin features (according to the Minimum feature size) of the model. If the Minimum perimeter width is thinner than the thickness of the feature, the perimeter will become as thick as the feature itself. If expressed as a percentage (for example 85%), it will be computed based on the nozzle diameter.

display_mirror_x.label: Mirror horizontally
display_mirror_x.tooltip: Enable horizontal mirroring of output images

display_mirror_y.label: Mirror vertically
display_mirror_y.tooltip: Enable vertical mirroring of output images

display_orientation.label: Display orientation
display_orientation.tooltip: Set the actual LCD display orientation inside the SLA printer. Portrait mode will flip the meaning of display width and height parameters and the output images will be rotated by 90 degrees.

high_viscosity_tilt_time.label: High viscosity
high_viscosity_tilt_time.tooltip: Time of the super slow tilt

area_fill.label: Area fill threshold
area_fill.tooltip: The value is expressed as a percentage of the bed area. If the area of a particular layer is smaller than 'area_fill', then 'Below area fill threshold' parameters are used to determine the layer separation (tearing) procedure. Otherwise 'Above area fill threshold' parameters are used.

relative_correction_x.label: Printer scaling correction in X axis
relative_correction_x.tooltip: Printer scaling correction in X axis

relative_correction_y.label: Printer scaling correction in Y axis
relative_correction_y.tooltip: Printer scaling correction in Y axis

relative_correction_z.label: Printer scaling correction in Z axis
relative_correction_z.tooltip: Printer scaling correction in Z axis

absolute_correction.label: Printer absolute correction
absolute_correction.tooltip: Will inflate or deflate the sliced 2D polygons according to the sign of the correction.

elefant_foot_min_width.label: Elephant foot minimum width
elefant_foot_min_width.tooltip: Minimum width of features to maintain when doing elephant foot compensation.

zcorrection_layers.label: Z compensation
zcorrection_layers.tooltip: Number of layers to Z correct to avoid cross layer bleed

gamma_correction.label: Printer gamma correction
gamma_correction.tooltip: This will apply a gamma correction to the rasterized 2D polygons. A gamma value of zero means thresholding with the threshold in the middle. This behaviour eliminates antialiasing without losing holes in polygons.

material_colour.label: Color
material_colour.tooltip: This is only used in the Slic3r interface as a visual help.

idle_temperature.label: Idle temperature
idle_temperature.tooltip: Nozzle temperature when the tool is currently not used in multi-tool setups.This is only used when 'Ooze prevention' is active in Print Settings.

faded_layers.label: Faded layers
faded_layers.tooltip: Number of the layers needed for the exposure time fade from initial exposure time to the exposure time

material_correction_x.label: Correction for expansion in X axis
material_correction_x.fullLabel: Correction for expansion in X axis
material_correction_x.tooltip: Correction for expansion in X axis

material_correction_y.label: Correction for expansion in Y axis
material_correction_y.fullLabel: Correction for expansion in Y axis
material_correction_y.tooltip: Correction for expansion in Y axis

material_correction_z.label: Correction for expansion in Z axis
material_correction_z.fullLabel: Correction for expansion in Z axis
material_correction_z.tooltip: Correction for expansion in Z axis

material_notes.label: SLA print material notes
material_notes.tooltip: You can put your notes regarding the SLA print material here.

default_sla_material_profile.label: Default SLA material profile
default_sla_material_profile.tooltip: Default print profile associated with the current printer profile. On selection of the current printer profile, this print profile will be activated.

default_sla_print_profile.label: Default SLA material profile
default_sla_print_profile.tooltip: Default print profile associated with the current printer profile. On selection of the current printer profile, this print profile will be activated.

support_enforcers_only.label: Support only in enforced regions
support_enforcers_only.tooltip: Only create support if it lies in a support enforcer.

support_points_density_relative.label: Support points density
support_points_density_relative.tooltip: This is a relative measure of support points density.

pad_enable.label: Use pad
pad_enable.tooltip: Add a pad underneath the supported model

pad_wall_thickness.label: Pad wall thickness
pad_wall_thickness.tooltip: The thickness of the pad and its optional cavity walls.

pad_wall_height.label: Pad wall height
pad_wall_height.tooltip: Defines the pad cavity depth. Set to zero to disable the cavity. Be careful when enabling this feature, as some resins may produce an extreme suction effect inside the cavity, which makes peeling the print off the vat foil difficult.

pad_brim_size.label: Pad brim size
pad_brim_size.tooltip: How far should the pad extend around the contained geometry

pad_max_merge_distance.label: Max merge distance
pad_max_merge_distance.tooltip: Some objects can get along with a few smaller pads instead of a single big one. This parameter defines how far the center of two smaller pads should be. If theyare closer, they will get merged into one pad.

pad_wall_slope.label: Pad wall slope
pad_wall_slope.tooltip: The slope of the pad wall relative to the bed plane. 90 degrees means straight walls.

pad_around_object.label: Pad around object
pad_around_object.tooltip: Create pad around object and ignore the support elevation

pad_object_gap.label: Pad object gap
pad_object_gap.tooltip: The gap between the object bottom and the generated pad in zero elevation mode.

pad_object_connector_stride.label: Pad object connector stride
pad_object_connector_stride.tooltip: Distance between two connector sticks which connect the object and the generated pad.

pad_object_connector_width.label: Pad object connector width
pad_object_connector_width.tooltip: Width of the connector sticks which connect the object and the generated pad.

pad_object_connector_penetration.label: Pad object connector penetration
pad_object_connector_penetration.tooltip: How much should the tiny connectors penetrate into the model body.

hollowing_enable.label: Enable hollowing
hollowing_enable.tooltip: Hollow out a model to have an empty interior

hollowing_min_thickness.label: Wall thickness
hollowing_min_thickness.tooltip: Minimum wall thickness of a hollowed model.

hollowing_quality.label: Accuracy
hollowing_quality.tooltip: Performance vs accuracy of calculation. Lower values may produce unwanted artifacts.

hollowing_closing_distance.label: Closing distance
hollowing_closing_distance.tooltip: Hollowing is done in two steps: first, an imaginary interior is calculated deeper (offset plus the closing distance) in the object and then it's inflated back to the specified offset. A greater closing distance makes the interior more rounded. At zero, the interior will resemble the exterior the most.

material_print_speed.label: Print speed
material_print_speed.tooltip: A slower printing profile might be necessary when using materials with higher viscosity or with some hollowed parts. It slows down the tilt movement and adds a delay before exposure.

sla_archive_format.label: Format of the output SLA archive
sla_archive_format.fullLabel: Format of the output SLA archive

delay_before_exposure.label: Delay before exposure
delay_before_exposure.tooltip: Delay before exposure after previous layer separation.

delay_after_exposure.label: Delay after exposure
delay_after_exposure.tooltip: Delay after exposure before layer separation.

tower_hop_height.label: Tower hop height
tower_hop_height.tooltip: The height of the tower raise.

tower_speed.label: Tower speed
tower_speed.tooltip: Tower speed used for tower raise.

tilt_down_initial_speed.label: Tilt down initial speed
tilt_down_initial_speed.tooltip: Tilt speed used for an initial portion of tilt down move.

tilt_down_finish_speed.label: Tilt down finish speed
tilt_down_finish_speed.tooltip: Tilt speed used for the rest of the tilt down move.

tilt_up_initial_speed.label: Tilt up initial speed
tilt_up_initial_speed.tooltip: Tilt speed used for an initial portion of tilt up move.

tilt_up_finish_speed.label: Tilt up finish speed
tilt_up_finish_speed.tooltip: Tilt speed used for the rest of the tilt-up.

use_tilt.label: Use tilt
use_tilt.tooltip: If enabled, tilt is used for layer separation. Otherwise, all the parameters below are ignored.

tilt_down_offset_steps.label: Tilt down offset steps
tilt_down_offset_steps.tooltip: Number of steps to move down from the calibrated (horizontal) position with 'tilt_down_initial_speed'.

tilt_down_offset_delay.label: Tilt down offset delay
tilt_down_offset_delay.tooltip: Delay after the tilt reaches 'tilt_down_offset_steps' position.

tilt_down_cycles.label: Tilt down cycles
tilt_down_cycles.tooltip: Number of cycles to split the rest of the tilt down move.

tilt_up_offset_steps.label: Tilt up offset steps
tilt_up_offset_steps.tooltip: Move tilt up to calibrated (horizontal) position minus this offset.

tilt_up_offset_delay.label: Tilt up offset delay
tilt_up_offset_delay.tooltip: Delay after the tilt reaches 'tilt_up_offset_steps' position.

tilt_up_cycles.label: Tilt up cycles
tilt_up_cycles.tooltip: Number of cycles to split the rest of the tilt-up.

load.label: Material preset name(s)
load.tooltip:
Name(s) of the material preset(s) used for slicing.
Could be filaments or sla_material preset name(s) depending on printer tochnology

help_fff.label: Help (FFF options)
help_fff.tooltip: Show the full list of print/G-code configuration options.

help_sla.label: Get list of print profiles and filament profiles for the selected printer profile
help_sla.fullLabel: Get list of print profiles and filament profiles for the selected printer profile
help_sla.tooltip:
Get list of print profiles and filament profiles for the selected 'printer-profile' into JSON.
Note:
To print out JSON into file use 'output' option.
To specify configuration folder use 'datadir' option.

gcodeviewer.label: G-code viewer
gcodeviewer.tooltip: Visualize an already sliced and saved G-code

save.label: Save config file
save.tooltip: Save configuration to the specified file.

info.label: Output Model Info
info.tooltip: Write information about the model to the console.

slice.label: Slice
slice.tooltip: Slice the model as FFF or SLA based on the printer_technology configuration value and export the result.

export_sla.label: Export SLA
export_sla.tooltip: Slice the model and export SLA printing layers as PNG.

export_gcode.label: Export G-code
export_gcode.tooltip: Slice the model and export toolpaths as G-code.

align_xy.label: Align XY
align_xy.tooltip: Align the model to the given point.

cut.label: Cut
cut.tooltip: Cut model at the given Z.

center.label: Center
center.tooltip: Center the print around the given center.

dont_arrange.label: Don't arrange
dont_arrange.tooltip: Do not rearrange the given models before merging and keep their original XY coordinates.

ensure_on_bed.label: Ensure on bed
ensure_on_bed.tooltip: Lift the object above the bed when it is partially below. Enabled by default, use --no-ensure-on-bed to disable.

duplicate_grid.label: Duplicate by grid
duplicate_grid.tooltip: Multiply copies by creating a grid.

merge.label: Merge
merge.tooltip: Arrange the supplied models in a plate and merge them in a single model in order to perform actions once.

rotate.label: Rotate
rotate.tooltip: Rotation angle around the Z axis in degrees.

rotate_x.label: Rotate around X
rotate_x.tooltip: Rotation angle around the X axis in degrees.

rotate_y.label: Rotate around Y
rotate_y.tooltip: Rotation angle around the Y axis in degrees.

split.label: Split
split.tooltip: Detect unconnected parts in the given model(s) and split them into separate objects.

scale_to_fit.label: Scale to Fit
scale_to_fit.tooltip: Scale to fit the given volume.

ignore_nonexistent_config.label: Ignore non-existent config files
ignore_nonexistent_config.tooltip: Do not fail if a file supplied to --load does not exist.

config_compatibility.label: Forward-compatibility rule when loading configurations from config files and project files (3MF, AMF).
config_compatibility.fullLabel: Forward-compatibility rule when loading configurations from config files and project files (3MF, AMF).
config_compatibility.tooltip: This version of preFlight may not understand configurations produced by the newest preFlight versions. For example, newer preFlight may extend the list of supported firmware flavors. One may decide to bail out or to substitute an unknown value with a default silently or verbosely.
enumLabels: Bail out on unknown configuration values
Enable reading unknown configuration values by verbosely substituting them with defaults.
Enable reading unknown configuration values by silently substituting them with defaults.

output.label: Output File
output.tooltip: The file where the output will be written (if not specified, it will be based on the input file).

datadir.label: Data directory
datadir.tooltip: Load and store settings at the given directory. This is useful for maintaining different profiles or including configurations from a network storage.

threads.label: Maximum number of threads
threads.tooltip: Sets the maximum number of threads the slicing process will use. If not defined, it will be decided automatically.

loglevel.label: Logging level
loglevel.tooltip:
Sets logging sensitivity. 0:fatal, 1:error, 2:warning, 3:info, 4:debug, 5:trace
For example. loglevel=2 logs fatal, error and warning level messages.

debug.label: OpenGL debug output
debug.tooltip: Activate OpenGL debug output on graphic cards which support it (OpenGL 4.3 or higher)

sw_renderer.label: Render with a software renderer
sw_renderer.tooltip: Render with a software renderer. The bundled MESA software renderer is loaded instead of the default OpenGL driver.

single_instance_on_url.label: Single instance mode for preflight url
single_instance_on_url.fullLabel: Single instance mode for preflight url
single_instance_on_url.tooltip: Works as single_instance but only if preflight url is present.

zhop.label: Current z-hop
zhop.tooltip: Contains z-hop present at the beginning of the custom G-code block.

position.label: Position
position.tooltip: Position of the extruder at the beginning of the custom G-code block. If the custom G-code travels somewhere else, it should write to this variable so preFlight knows where it travels from when it gets control back.

e_retracted.label: Retraction
e_retracted.tooltip: Retraction state at the beginning of the custom G-code block. If the custom G-code moves the extruder axis, it should write to this variable so preFlight deretracts correctly when it gets control back.

e_restart_extra.label: Extra deretraction
e_restart_extra.tooltip: Currently planned extra extruder priming after deretraction.

e_position.label: Absolute E position
e_position.tooltip: Current position of the extruder axis. Only used with absolute extruder addressing.

current_extruder.label: Current extruder
current_extruder.tooltip: Zero-based index of currently used extruder.

current_object_idx.label: Current object index
current_object_idx.tooltip: Specific for sequential printing. Zero-based index of currently printed object.

has_single_extruder_multi_material_primi.label: Has single extruder MM priming
has_single_extruder_multi_material_primi.tooltip: Are the extra multi-material priming regions used in this print?

has_wipe_tower.label: Has wipe tower
has_wipe_tower.tooltip: Whether or not wipe tower is being generated in the print.

initial_extruder.label: Initial extruder
initial_extruder.tooltip: Zero-based index of the first extruder used in the print. Same as initial_tool.

initial_filament_type.label: Initial filament type
initial_filament_type.tooltip: String containing filament type of the first used extruder.

initial_tool.label: Initial tool
initial_tool.tooltip: Zero-based index of the first extruder used in the print. Same as initial_extruder.

is_extruder_used.label: Is extruder used?
is_extruder_used.tooltip: Vector of booleans stating whether a given extruder is used in the print.

extruded_volume.label: Volume per extruder
extruded_volume.tooltip: Total filament volume extruded per extruder during the entire print.

normal_print_time.label: Print time (normal mode)
normal_print_time.tooltip: Estimated print time when printed in normal mode (i.e. not in silent mode). Same as print_time.

num_printing_extruders.label: Number of printing extruders
num_printing_extruders.tooltip: Number of extruders used during the print.

print_time.label: Print time (normal mode)
print_time.tooltip: Estimated print time when printed in normal mode (i.e. not in silent mode). Same as normal_print_time.

printing_filament_types.label: Used filament types
printing_filament_types.tooltip: Comma-separated list of all filament types used during the print.

silent_print_time.label: Print time (silent mode)
silent_print_time.tooltip: Estimated print time when printed in silent mode.

total_cost.label: Total cost
total_cost.tooltip: Total cost of all material used in the print. Calculated from cost in Filament Settings.

total_weight.label: Total weight
total_weight.tooltip: Total weight of the print. Calculated from density in Filament Settings.

total_wipe_tower_cost.label: Total wipe tower cost
total_wipe_tower_cost.tooltip: Total cost of the material wasted on the wipe tower. Calculated from cost in Filament Settings.

total_wipe_tower_filament.label: Wipe tower volume
total_wipe_tower_filament.tooltip: Total filament volume extruded on the wipe tower.

used_filament.label: Used filament
used_filament.tooltip: Total length of filament used in the print.

total_toolchanges.label: Total number of toolchanges
total_toolchanges.tooltip: Number of toolchanges during the print.

extruded_volume_total.label: Total volume
extruded_volume_total.tooltip: Total volume of filament used during the entire print.

extruded_weight.label: Weight per extruder
extruded_weight.tooltip: Weight per extruder extruded during the entire print. Calculated from density in Filament Settings.

extruded_weight_total.label: Total weight
extruded_weight_total.tooltip: Total weight of the print. Calculated from density in Filament Settings.

total_layer_count.label: Total layer count
total_layer_count.tooltip: Number of layers in the entire print.

num_objects.label: Number of objects
num_objects.tooltip: Total number of objects in the print.

num_instances.label: Number of instances
num_instances.tooltip: Total number of object instances in the print, summed over all objects.

input_filename_base.label: Input filename without extension
input_filename_base.tooltip: Source filename of the first object, without extension.

first_layer_print_convex_hull.label: First layer convex hull
first_layer_print_convex_hull.tooltip: Vector of points of the first layer convex hull. Each element has the following format: '[x, y]' (x and y are floating-point numbers in mm).

first_layer_print_min.label: Bottom-left corner of first layer bounding box
first_layer_print_min.fullLabel: Bottom-left corner of first layer bounding box

first_layer_print_max.label: Top-right corner of first layer bounding box
first_layer_print_max.fullLabel: Top-right corner of first layer bounding box

first_layer_print_size.label: Size of the first layer bounding box
first_layer_print_size.fullLabel: Size of the first layer bounding box

print_bed_min.label: Bottom-left corner of print bed bounding box
print_bed_min.fullLabel: Bottom-left corner of print bed bounding box

print_bed_max.label: Top-right corner of print bed bounding box
print_bed_max.fullLabel: Top-right corner of print bed bounding box

print_bed_size.label: Size of the print bed bounding box
print_bed_size.fullLabel: Size of the print bed bounding box

timestamp.label: Timestamp
timestamp.tooltip: String containing current time in yyyyMMdd-hhmmss format.

num_extruders.label: Number of extruders
num_extruders.tooltip: Total number of extruders, regardless of whether they are used in the current print.

print_preset.label: Print preset name
print_preset.tooltip: Name of the print preset used for slicing.

filament_preset.label: Filament preset name
filament_preset.tooltip: Names of the filament presets used for slicing. The variable is a vector containing one name for each extruder.

printer_preset.label: Printer preset name
printer_preset.tooltip: Name of the printer preset used for slicing.

physical_printer_preset.label: Physical printer name
physical_printer_preset.tooltip: Name of the physical printer used for slicing.

layer_num.label: Layer number
layer_num.tooltip: Zero-based index of the current layer (i.e. first layer is number 0).

layer_z.label: Layer Z
layer_z.tooltip: Height of the current layer above the print bed, measured to the top of the layer.

max_layer_z.label: Maximal layer Z
max_layer_z.tooltip: Height of the last layer above the print bed.

filament_extruder_id.label: Current extruder index
filament_extruder_id.tooltip: Zero-based index of currently used extruder (i.e. first extruder has index 0).

previous_extruder.label: Previous extruder
previous_extruder.tooltip: Index of the extruder that is being unloaded. The index is zero based (first extruder has index 0).

next_extruder.label: Next extruder
next_extruder.tooltip: Index of the extruder that is being loaded. The index is zero based (first extruder has index 0).

toolchange_z.label: Toolchange Z
toolchange_z.tooltip: Height above the print bed when the toolchange takes place. Usually the same as layer_z, but can be different.

color_change_extruder.label: Color change extruder
color_change_extruder.tooltip: Index of the extruder for which color change will be performed. The index is zero based (first extruder has index 0).

filament_retract_length.label: Retraction length
filament_retract_length.tooltip: When retraction is triggered, filament is pulled back by the specified amount (the length is measured on raw filament, before it enters the extruder).

filament_retract_lift_above.label: Above Z
filament_retract_lift_above.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place above the specified absolute Z. You can tune this setting for skipping lift on the first layers.

filament_retract_lift_below.label: Below Z
filament_retract_lift_below.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place below the specified absolute Z. You can tune this setting for limiting lift to the first layers.

filament_retract_speed.label: Retraction Speed
filament_retract_speed.tooltip: The speed for retractions (it only applies to the extruder motor).

filament_travel_max_lift.label: Maximum ramping lift
filament_travel_max_lift.tooltip: Maximum lift height of the ramping lift. It may not be reached if the next position is close to the old one.

filament_deretract_speed.label: Deretraction Speed
filament_deretract_speed.tooltip: The speed for loading of a filament into extruder after retraction (it only applies to the extruder motor). If left to zero, the retraction speed is used.

filament_retract_restart_extra.label: Deretraction extra length
filament_retract_restart_extra.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after the travel move, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament. This setting is rarely needed.

filament_retract_before_travel.label: Minimum travel after retraction
filament_retract_before_travel.tooltip: Retraction is not triggered when travel moves are shorter than this length.

filament_retract_length_toolchange.label: Length
filament_retract_length_toolchange.tooltip: When retraction is triggered before changing tool, filament is pulled back by the specified amount (the length is measured on raw filament, before it enters the extruder).

filament_retract_restart_extra_toolchang.label: Extra length on restart
filament_retract_restart_extra_toolchang.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after changing tool, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament.

filament_retract_layer_change.label: Retract on layer change
filament_retract_layer_change.tooltip: This flag enforces a retraction whenever a Z move is done.

filament_wipe.label: Wipe while retracting
filament_wipe.tooltip: This flag will move the nozzle while retracting to minimize the possible blob on leaky extruders.

filament_wipe_extend.label: Extend wipe
filament_wipe_extend.tooltip: When enabled, the wipe move continues in the same direction as the last extrusion move. When disabled (default), the wipe follows the perimeter loop for the duration of the move.

filament_travel_lift_before_obstacle.label: Steeper ramp before obstacles
filament_travel_lift_before_obstacle.tooltip: If enabled, preFlight detects obstacles along the travel path and makes the slope steeper in case an obstacle might be hit during the initial phase of the travel.

filament_travel_ramping_lift.label: Use ramping lift
filament_travel_ramping_lift.tooltip: Generates a ramping lift instead of lifting the extruder directly upwards. The travel is split into two phases: the ramp and the standard horizontal travel. This option helps reduce stringing.

filament_wipe_length.label: Wipe length
filament_wipe_length.tooltip: Length of the wipe move. When using firmware retraction or without 'Wipe while retracting', the wipe will be a pure travel move (no retraction). Set to 0 to use the default wipe behavior based on retraction length.

filament_retract_before_wipe.label: Retract amount before wipe
filament_retract_before_wipe.tooltip: With bowden extruders, it may be wise to do some amount of quick retract before doing the wipe movement.

filament_travel_slope.label: Ramping slope angle
filament_travel_slope.tooltip: Slope of the ramp in the initial phase of the travel.

filament_seam_gap_distance.label: Seam gap distance
filament_seam_gap_distance.tooltip: The distance between the endpoints of a closed loop perimeter. Positive values will shorten and interrupt the loop slightly to reduce the seam. Negative values will extend the loop, causing the endpoints to overlap slightly. When percents are used, the distance is derived from the nozzle diameter. Set to zero to disable this feature.
